data.article_summary: Xenharmlib 0.3.0 是一个支持传统和非传统音乐理论的Python库，特别适用于非十二平均律系统的微音程和宏音程调音。它易于使用且可扩展，支持西方和非西方音阶系统、非标准记谱法以及音程、音阶的分析与调制建议。该库还提供对波尔-皮尔斯调音的群论分析等功能。Xenharmlib 并非用于乐谱编写或合成，而是专注于和声关系的科学探索，采用函数式编程原则，对象为不可变类型。未来计划包括支持更多记谱法、高级后调性分析和Just Intonation等。该库基于GNU Public License v3发布，源代码托管于Gitlab，并有Discord社区支持。

New Release
Xenharmlib 0.3.0 has just been released.
Find out what’s new
Welcome to xenharmlib’s documentation!
¶
Xenharmonic (adj.):
Pertaining to music which sounds unlike
that composed in the familiar 12 tone equal-tempered scale.
—
Ivor Darreg
Xenharmlib is a generalized music theory library that supports traditional
Western and non-western harmonic systems, unconventional microtonal and
macrotonal tunings, diatonic and posttonal set theory and non-standard
notations.

Audience & Design Philosophy
¶
Xenharmlib is targeted at composers and researchers who already have
basic knowledge in python programming.
Xenharmlib does
not
aim to be a score composition tool, sequencer,
or synthesizer (however it is possible to build such things on top of
it). Rather it wants to provide a toolset for exploring different
concepts of harmonic relations with a scientific focus.
Xenharmlib is object-oriented but mostly designed around functional
programming principles: Objects are considered immutable and methods
do not alter internal states but return modified versions of the
original object.
Features
¶
A selection of things supported by xenharmlib:
Equal division tunings (e.g. Western, Modern Arabic, Turkish Makam,
Bohlen-Pierce, Wendy Carlos’ Gamma Scale)
Western notation (including interval naming)
Up/Down notation (a superset of Western notation)
Analysis of intervals, scales, and their relations to one another
Group theoretical analysis (integer pitches, pitch classes, etc)
Interval sequence pattern matching
Modulation suggestions for arbitrary key changes
Basic posttonal analysis (normal & prime form calculations, inversion, etc)
Roadmap
¶
A list of planned features (not necessarily in chronological order):
Templates for Western music
Plugin interface for score rendering backends
Advanced posttonal analysis (interval vectors, z-Relations, Forte numbers)
Rothenberg propriety and interval matrices
MOS scale generation utilities
Just Intonation and prime limit tunings
Extended Helmholtz-Ellis JI Pitch Notation
Odd Limit Tunings
Arel-Ezgi-Uzdilek notation
License
¶
Xenharmlib is released under the
GNU Public License v3
.
You can find the source code hosted on
Gitlab.com
Acknowledgments
¶
Thanks to
Kite Giedraitis
and
Lumi Pakkanen
and everyone else on the
Xenharmonic Alliance Discord who was patient with me when I was
struggling to implement UpDownNotation.
Support and Contact
¶
If you want to ask for a new feature or report a bug, take it to the
Gitlab issue page
.
In case you just wanna chat with the maintainer: I often hang around on
the
Xenharmonic Alliance Discord
under the name
@retooth

In the following, you will find a guide to most of xenharmlib’s

data.title: RapidRAW: A non-destructive and GPU-accelerated RAW image editor
data.author: l8rlump
data.article_summary: RapidRAW是一款现代、高性能、非破坏性的RAW图像编辑器，支持GPU加速，体积小巧（不到30MB），适用于Windows、macOS和Linux。它由CyberTimon开发，旨在为摄影工作流提供高效工具，同时加深对React和Rust的理解。其核心功能包括GPU加速处理、AI驱动的遮罩、广泛的RAW格式支持、非破坏性编辑、32位精度、专业的调整工具（如色调控制、颜色分级、细节增强等）、以及高效的图像库管理。近期更新包括增强的AI功能、图像评分过滤器、预设覆盖、以及对ComfyUI的初步集成。项目采用AGPL-3.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于开源RAW图像处理工具“RawTherapee”的评价与讨论，涉及功能、性能、用户体验、技术细节等方面。

不同观点：
• **对RawTherapee的积极评价**：
   - strogonoff：赞赏其色彩科学准确性、可脚本化、丰富的文档（RawPedia），尤其适合对技术细节感兴趣的用户。同时也指出其缺少HDR输出的问题。
   - miladyincontrol：希望加入亮度蒙版功能，认为这对RAW编辑非常重要。对现有的AI主体蒙版功能表示赞赏。
   - ioma8：表示有兴趣参与该项目的开发。

• **性能问题的反馈**：
   - polishdude20：在M1 Mac上运行时，初次加载卡顿严重，虽然之后有所改善，但整体不够流畅。
   - vsviridov：在Windows 10和AMD RX 6900 XT上运行时，处理6000x4000的DNG文件速度很慢，调整参数时延迟明显。

• **对元数据和跨平台支持的关注**：
   - pradn：关心元数据的存储方式，尤其是是否为开放格式，以便在不同程序间迁移编辑内容。同时提到不愿每月付费订阅Lightroom。
   - rkagerer：询问系统要求和最低操作系统版本。

• **对用户界面和技术实现的讨论**：
   - dxroshan：认为基于网页的图像编辑界面不好，会慢且资源消耗大。
   - Springtime：赞赏README中的视觉概览，但指出GIF文件过大，建议使用视频代替以提高加载速度。
   - bjelkeman-again：询问Mac代码签名的难度。

• **对RAW和Bitmap区别的疑问**：
   - brcmthrowaway：询问RAW和Bitmap的区别，特别提到Bitmap是否无压缩。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户对RawTherapee的技术细节表现出浓厚兴趣（如色彩科学、元数据处理、默认相机和镜头配置文件等），而另一些用户则更关注实际使用中的性能问题（如卡顿、延迟）。
• 关于跨平台支持和系统要求的问题也被多次提及，显示出用户群体对软件兼容性和易用性的关注。
• 部分用户对RawTherapee与商业软件（如Capture One、Lightroom）的对比，反映出开源与商业软件之间的选择争议。

RapidRAW
A beautiful, non-destructive, and GPU-accelerated RAW image editor built with performance in mind.
RapidRAW is a modern, high-performance alternative to Adobe Lightroom. It delivers a feature-rich, beautiful editing experience in a lightweight package (under 30MB) for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
I developed this project as a personal challenge at the age of 18. My goal was to create a high-performance tool for my own photography workflow while deepening my understanding of both React and Rust, with the support from Google Gemini.
Have fun!

Key Features
Core Editing Engine
GPU-Accelerated Processing:
All image adjustments are processed on the GPU using a custom WGSL shader for rapid feedback.
Masking:
Instantly create precise masks with AI subject and foreground detection. Combine with traditional Brush, Linear, and Radial masks for great control.
Generative Edits:
Remove objects or add new elements with text prompts. Each edit creates a non-destructive patch layer, powered by an optional ComfyUI backend.
Full RAW Support:
Supports a wide range of RAW camera formats thanks to rawler.
Non-Destructive Workflow:
All edits are stored in a
.rrdata
sidecar file, leaving your original images untouched.
32-bit Precision:
Ensures high-quality adjustments without banding or data loss.
Professional Grade Adjustments
Tonal Controls:
Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, and Blacks.
Tone Curves:
Full control over Luma, Red, Green, and Blue channels.
Color Grading:
Temperature, Tint, Vibrance, Saturation, and a full HSL color mixer.
Detail Enhancement:
Sharpening, Clarity, Structure, and Noise Reduction.
Effects:
Dehaze, Vignette, and realistic Film Grain simulation.
Transform Tools:
Crop with aspect ratio locking, Rotate, and Flip.
Library & Workflow
Image Library:
Effortlessly sort, rate, and manage your entire photo collection for a streamlined and efficient workflow.
Folder Management:
Integrated folder tree, create, rename, and delete folders directly within the app.
File Operations:
Copy, move, and duplicate images and their associated edits.
Filmstrip View:
Quickly navigate between all the images in your current folder while editing.
Batch Operations:
Save significant time by applying a consistent set of adjustments or exporting entire batches of images simultaneously.
EXIF Data Viewer:
Gain insights by inspecting the complete metadata from your camera, including shutter speed, aperture, ISO, and lens information.
Productivity & UI
Preset System:
Create, save, import, and export your favorite looks.

• **对元数据和跨平台支持的关注**：
   - pradn：关心元数据的存储方式，尤其是是否为开放格式，以便在不同程序间迁移编辑内容。同时提到不愿每月付费订阅Lightroom。
   - rkagerer：询问系统要求和最低操作系统版本。

• **对用户界面和技术实现的讨论**：
   - dxroshan：认为基于网页的图像编辑界面不好，会慢且资源消耗大。
   - Springtime：赞赏README中的视觉概览，但指出GIF文件过大，建议使用视频代替以提高加载速度。
   - bjelkeman-again：询问Mac代码签名的难度。

data.title: Frame of preference A history of Mac settings, 1984–2004
data.author: K7PJP
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了1984年至2004年间Mac电脑设置界面的演变历史。作者作为一名设计师，虽然按理应不喜欢设置选项，但作为用户却对其充满兴趣，并每年设立“设置日”来研究软件中的选项和开关。文章特别提到1984年由Susan Kare设计的Mac控制面板，这一设计至今仍被提及。最初的控制面板简洁直观，包含了动画和早期GUI实验元素，如滑块和步进器。有趣的是，当时团队对桌面定制功能存在分歧，担心用户会创建“丑陋的桌面图案”。尽管存在一些小瑕疵和操作缓慢的问题，早期控制面板依然充满魅力。到了1986年，随着时间推移，许多原有的 charm 逐渐消失。文章通过回顾Mac设置界面的发展，展示了这台机器早期历史和设计挑战。

44505171.article_content:
Frame of preference
A history of Mac settings, 1984â2004
As a designer, Iâm meant to dislike settings. As a user, I love them.
Every year I celebrate Settings Day: a day when I take a look at the options and toggles in all the apps I use. I do this out of curiosity â what was added since the last time I looked? â but also because I love this way of getting to know software: peeking under the hood, walking the back alleys, learning what has been tricky or important enough to be equipped with a checkbox.
During the last Settings Day, I had a realization that the totemic 1984 Mac control panel, designed by Susan Kare, is still to this day perhaps the only settings screen ever brought up in casual conversation.
I kept wondering about that screen, and about what happened since then. Turns out, the Mac settings have lived a far more fascinating life than I imagined, have been redesigned many times, and can tell us a lot about the early history and the troubled upbringing of this interesting machine.
Join me on a journey through the first twenty years of Macâs control panels.
1984
Itâs rare when software matches hardware so well.
Even already in 1979, the Macintosh was envisioned as a home appliance akin to a toaster or a TV. This was documented in
one of my favorite memos of all time
. Get the machine out of the box. Leave the screwdriver in the drawer. There is no step three.
Once you do that,
open the Apple menu
, and then
launch the Control Panel
, and you will find a small appliance hiding inside the machine, too. A European appliance, even âÂ outside of the title bar, there are absolutely no words present here.
The Control Panel is a handsome and tight design, put together by Susan Kare as the
last desk accessory
, just weeks before the Macâs announcement. It feels alive, depicting a perhaps surprising amount of movement sometimes via animation, sometimes via comic book-inspired conventions: soundwaves exiting the speaker, menus blinking upon activation, a finger pressing a key, the mouse rolling on the desk. Itâs also a playground of sorts for early GUI experiments: there is an early
slider
here, some
steppers
for date and time, a custom cursor, and a mini map showing a miniature desktop.
The last two are in service of the most contentious addition:
customizing the desktop pattern
. The original Mac team was divided on this one, worrying this would lead to âabominable patternsâ and therefore âugly desktopsâ â an ongoing design challenge for any setting that is not about how something works, but about how something
looks
.
Future, more garish desktop options on computers and eventually smartphones would render these early reservations quaint. This might be the best that the Mac desktop will look for about the next twenty years. But at this moment, it felt serious. The creator of
MacPaint
rebelled and built his app so that any custom background would be drawn over by a default 50% checkerboard anyway. But can you even make an ugly desktop pattern with just 64 black pixels to mess with? Maybeâ¦ The most surprising is the fact that the team also prepared 41 beautiful built-in patterns, but hid them inside this control panel with the only hints how to get them appearing in the manual.
At this point in time, this was the only way you could truly customize your Mac to fit your personality, and itâs nice that it also happens to be one thatâs fun to use, ironically perhaps inspired by MacPaint and its
FatBits
setting.
Other controls might be slightly surprising: out of just ten settings, three are dedicated to motor memory. The two keyboard toggles make sense. Even in the early 1980s, there were keyboards â terminals or electric typewriters â whose repeating style you might have gotten used to. We already knew that once something lodges itself in your fingertips, itâs really hard to override it, even consciously, so it was clever to add customization to work around that.
But the third option is for double clicking that never existed before. There werenât really decades or even years of studies done on mouse usage, either. I imagine the creators felt it was better safe than sorry.
This early Control Panel has been celebrated since, even though there are mistakes here: the inconsistent Chicago 3, the top section being one pixel too short, and an occasional uneven border. The UI, like the whole Mac, is slow and clunky â you can see the panel, the windows, even the menus struggling to be drawn with required haste. (Only the mouse pointer is speedy, and it was
a small miracle
how it got this way.)
For people using this early Mac, this was likely frustrating as hell. Today, it feels like a perfect intro for a new little machine, the best dense collection of pixels this side of
Winamp
. Itâs cute, it gets the job done, and it has tons of charm.
Control Panel embroidery
Stitched and patterned by
gmatom
1986
Two years later, and a lot of that charm is gone. Susan Kare and Steve Jo

data.title: SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty service to meet surging demand
data.author: saubeidl
data.article_summary: SUSE推出了一项名为"Sovereign Premium Support"的新服务，旨在帮助欧洲企业和政府在其IT基础设施中实现数字主权。该服务确保所有支持人员和数据都位于欧盟境内，客户支持数据存储在欧盟的网络和服务器上，且只有欧盟工作人员能访问敏感数据。此举响应了欧盟对数据隐私和独立性的日益关注，特别是面对非欧盟国家，尤其是美国公司的数据控制风险。SUSE的这项服务专为需要严格数据驻留和操作控制的组织设计，如国防、政府和执法部门，但也面向所有欧洲组织开放。这项服务在当前地缘政治不确定性增加的背景下，为欧洲客户提供了更强的安全保障和业务连续性支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕SUSE Linux、数据主权和欧洲数字主权的讨论

不同观点：
• [pjmlp] 认为FOSS（自由和开源软件）操作系统可能是摆脱美国主导的消费级操作系统及相关编程语言的唯一出路。他提到自己曾是Linux的狂热爱好者，对Linux发行版的碎片化以及桌面环境的梦想破灭感到失望，但特别指出SuSE和KDE的整合曾给他留下深刻印象。

• [jpalomaki] 强调仅仅关注服务器位置（如“存储在欧盟网络和服务器上”）并不足够，关键是谁在管理和控制这些服务器和网络。他认为讨论数据主权时，管理权比物理位置更重要。

• [0xfedcafe] 对SUSE在欧洲的被忽视表示不解，指出SUSE已经具备几乎所有必要的工具（如Rancher和openSUSE），并且在欧洲有相当的知名度。他对欧洲数字主权讨论中倾向于选择美国项目（如Fedora）而非SUSE表示质疑。

• [defraudbah] 对欧洲数据主权持怀疑态度，认为通过更多法规未必能赢得这场“战争”。他提到德国的先例，认为即使丹麦有可能迁移到Linux，最终可能也会像德国一样反复。同时，他对未来十年是否会有实质性改变表示悲观，预测只会出现更多补助和法律，但不会有根本性变化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到SUSE的历史和其在欧洲的知名度，特别是其与KDE的整合及在开源项目中的地位。
• 数据主权的定义和实现方式存在争议，焦点在于服务器位置与管理权的相对重要性。
• 对欧洲是否能够真正实现数字主权存在不同看法，有人持乐观态度，认为SUSE是合适选择，而有人则持怀疑态度，认为法规和政策变化难以带来实际效果。

44507166.article_content:
Business
Home
Business
Enterprise Software
SUSE launches new European digital sovereignty support service to meet surging demand
With SUSE's help, European companies and governments can ensure their IT support, software, and data assets are safe.
Written by
Steven Vaughan-Nichols,
Senior Contributing Editor
Senior Contributing Editor
July 8, 2025 at 12:00 a.m. PT
Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images
Wary of the US government and tech companies, the European Union (EU) has seen a surge in support for
open source
and
Linux
. In the last few months, local EU governments,
including the city of Lyon in France,
the
German state of Schleswig-Holstein
, and
Denmark,
have begun their move to Linux and open-source software from
Microsoft Windows
and Office. Now, Luxembourg-based European open-source powerhouse
SUSE
is offering extensive support to businesses and governments that want to keep their IT infrastructure inside the European Union.
Also:
7 things every Linux beginner should know before downloading their first distro
The
Digital Sovereignty
movement is a big deal in Europe for a reason. Today, over 90% of European data resides on servers operated by non-EU and primarily American companies. This dependency exposes EU entities to data privacy, economic leverage, and potential risks of foreign surveillance.
As a result, according to tech researcher IDC,
84% of European organizations using cloud technologies are either currently using or planning to use sovereign cloud solutions
. Rahiel Nasir, IDC's research director for European Cloud Strategies, described 2025 as a "watershed year," with growing geopolitical and economic uncertainties putting digital sovereignty at the forefront for organizations.
Also:
Linux's remarkable journey from one dev's hobby to 40 million lines of code - and counting
That's why SUSE, a global leader in enterprise open-source solutions, has announced the launch of its Sovereign Premium Support package. This comprehensive support service is designed to meet the growing demand for digital sovereignty.
Specifically, Dirk-Peter (DP) van Leeuwen, SUSE's CEO, explained: "For some, it's a brand new story. But for us,
digital sovereignty
is old news. We've been enabling it for years for our customers. Along the way, we've learned you have to get three main things right: Data, technology, and operations. The last area -- business operations -- is often least looked at, but it's often the hardest to deliver. Ultimately, it is about the people -- where are they? And how do we ensure we have the scale to deliver business continuity? That's what we're addressing with the launch of SUSE Sovereign Premium Support."
Also:
I put Linux on this 8-inch mini laptop, and unlocked a new way of computing
In practice, SUSE's Sovereign Premium Support is tailored for enterprises and public sector organizations that require strict data residency, privacy, and operational control within the EU. The service ensures that:
All support personnel and data are based in the EU, with named premium support engineers and service delivery managers assigned to each customer.
Customer support data is stored exclusively on EU-located networks and servers, addressing both regulatory and geopolitical concerns.
Access to sensitive data is strictly limited to EU-based staff, with a commitment to encrypting all data required for troubleshooting.
This approach directly responds to the evolving landscape of European regulations and the heightened focus on digital independence. While it's an approach meant specifically for areas such as defense, government, and law enforcement, where compliance and resilience are paramount, it's being offered to all European organizations.
As Udo Wuertz, CDO and fellow at the data center company
Fsas Technologies Europe
, said, SUSE's "Open by Design, Sovereign by Choice" philosophy, combined with enhanced EU-based support, provides tailored solutions for customers with stringent sovereignty requirements.
Also:
Can't upgrade your Windows 10 PC? Here are your options before it all ends in 3 months
If this focus sounds paranoid, well, the world has changed. There's more geopolitical uncertainty today than since the Cold War threatened to get hot. So, for Europeans, SUSE's new program may be just what they need to feel secure again. SUSE stands ready to help with its Linux, open-source, and cloud offerings.
Contact SUSE
to learn more about their latest service.

data.article_summary: iPodLinux是一个将Linux系统移植到iPod设备的开源项目。该项目已成功将定制版的uClinux内核移植到1至3代iPod，并开发了名为podzilla的用户界面，增加了Apple固件不具备的功能。目前项目仍在开发后续iPod型号的支持，包括第四代、mini、Nano和Video等。用户可通过官方安装程序安装iPodLinux，并可在项目状态页或博客追踪进展。对于新硬件的支持，项目接受捐赠。高级用户可在不受官方支持的设备上尝试安装，但风险自负。

不同观点：

• [theturtle] 提到自己多年前在iPod上安装了项目，但现在找不到该设备。

Welcome to the home of the

iPodLinux is an open source venture into porting Linux onto the iPod
(
https://www.apple.com/ipod/
)
.
So far, we have successfully ported a customized uClinux
(
http://www.uclinux.org

Additional

and

generation

Donations

Project Status
page or the blog.

provide support
for these newer iPods.

data.title: Tree Borrows
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Rust编程语言中用于处理不安全代码的新模型——Tree Borrows。Rust以其基于所有权的类型系统著称，提供内存安全和数据竞争自由等强保证，但“不安全”代码块需手动维护安全。为确保编译器优化正确性，需明确定义何为“不良”不安全代码。先前模型Stacked Borrows设定了相关规则，但排除了现实中常见的一些模式，且未考虑Rust借用检查器的最新高级功能。Tree Borrows通过将Stacked Borrows的栈结构替换为树结构，解决了这些问题，减少了被拒绝的测试案例数量，并证明能保留大部分优化，还支持新的优化如读-读重排。该研究获得了PLDI'25的杰出论文奖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust的借用检查机制及其变种（如Tree Borrows和Stacked Borrows）在编译器优化和处理不安全代码方面的应用和挑战。

不同观点：
• **kibwen** 分享了Ralf Jung关于Rust操作语义的详细博客和演讲，提供了有关Rust语义精确规格的背景，特别是如何在可执行形式中实现这些语义。
• **jcalvinowens** 质疑编译器是否真的能从Rust的类型系统中获得强大的优化能力，提到Linux之父Torvalds对C语言中的严格别名规则的批评，并询问Rust是否真的与C有根本不同，尤其是在使用`unsafe`时。
• **Voultapher** 赞赏Tree Borrows模型，认为它解决了某些棘手的问题，并且在其实践中发现Tree Borrows允许一些在Stacked Borrows下非法的代码。
• **fuhsnn** 提出未来编程语言是否会允许不同的借用检查器实现，以在编译速度、运行速度和算法灵活性等方面提供选择。
• **vollbrecht** 测试了论文中的示例代码，发现当前稳定版的Rust编译器并没有如论文所述拒绝某些代码。
• **wavemode** 对论文中关于不安全代码的描述提出异议，认为使用指针共存多个可变引用是未定义行为，并对论文的观点表示困惑。

补充讨论：
• **chombier** 提供了PLDI会议的另一个相关演讲链接。
• **pvg** 提到Stacked Borrows在2018和2020年的讨论线程。
• **nixpulvis** 提供了Miri中Stacked Borrows实现的链接。
• **pil0u** 提到论文作者之一的Neven Villani是著名数学家Cédric Villani的儿子。
• **gavinhoward** 表示会将此模型应用到自己的编程语言中。
• **Nurbek-F** 感觉这个帖子每隔2-3个月就会出现一次，似有 déjà vu 的感觉。
• **olddustytrail** 以幽默的方式引用《魔戒》中的台词来评论Tree Borrows。

争议焦点：
• Rust的借用检查机制（特别是Tree Borrows和Stacked Borrows）在处理不安全代码时的有效性和一致性问题。
• 编译器是否能从Rust的类型系统中获得强大的优化能力，特别是在与C语言的比较中。
• 关于不安全代码的行为和未定义行为的理解差异。

Tree Borrows
external page
Neven Villani
,
external page
Johannes Hostert
,
external page
Derek Dreyer
,
external page
Ralf Jung
The state machine at the heart of Tree Borrows.
The Rust programming language is well known for its ownership-based type system, which offers strong guarantees like memory safety and data race freedom. However, Rust also provides
unsafe
escape hatches, for which safety is not guaranteed automatically and must instead be manually upheld by the programmer. This creates a tension. On the one hand, compilers would like to exploit the strong guarantees of the type system—particularly those pertaining to aliasing of pointers—in order to unlock powerful intraprocedural optimizations. On the other hand, those optimizations are easily invalidated by "badly behaved" unsafe code. To ensure correctness of such optimizations, it thus becomes necessary to clearly define what unsafe code is "badly behaved." In prior work,
external page
Stacked Borrows
defined a set of rules achieving this goal. However, Stacked Borrows rules out several patterns that turn out to be common in real-world unsafe Rust code, and it does not account for advanced features of the Rust borrow checker that were introduced more recently.
To resolve these issues, we present
Tree Borrows
. As the name suggests, Tree Borrows is defined by replacing the stack at the heart of Stacked Borrows with a tree. This overcomes the aforementioned limitations: our evaluation on the 30 000 most widely used Rust crates shows that Tree Borrows rejects 54% fewer test cases than Stacked Borrows does. Additionally, we prove (in Rocq) that it retains most of the Stacked Borrows optimizations and also enables important new ones, notably read-read reorderings.

data.title: A fast 3D collision detection algorithm
data.author: OlympicMarmoto
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GJK算法及其在物理引擎中的应用，包括数值误差处理、特殊情况处理和几何分解问题。

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为GJK算法在处理凸壳距离问题时需要关注数值误差，特别是在处理非唯一解的情况下，例如立方体放在立方体上时会出现的面对面接触问题。他还提到平坦多边形表面的细分问题会导致算法循环，并指出Stephen Cameron在1990年代的研究解决了部分问题。此外，他提到近似的凸分解算法可以生成更干净的几何形状，但需要从干净的几何开始。
• [ttw44] 表示对独立游戏开发中有关复杂物理引擎的资料稀缺的担忧，认为这些知识往往只在行业内或GitHub上能找到。
• [msteffen] 对数学推导中的两个等价命题感到困惑，特别是关于‘d’的定义和使用，担心如果‘d’过大可能导致错误的解。
• [leoqa] 提到分离轴定理（Sep Axis Theorem）作为一个简单易解释的算法，可以用于面试中解释给非技术人员听，并描述了其在碰撞检测中的应用。
• [reactordev] 关注非球形形状的处理，指出在处理大量顶点时碰撞检测的复杂性，并强调任何减少光线测试或剪裁的优化都是有价值的。

补充讨论：
• [socalgal2] 提供了相关的讨论链接，指向几日前的一个讨论。
• [EGreg] 提到自己在25年前就写过相关主题的文章，并提供了链接。
• [double051] 识别出评论中提到的测试案例是Halo 2中的Ascension。
• [MortyWaves] 抱怨Hacker News上提交的链接常常带有cookie垃圾信息。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在[msteffen]对数学推导的疑问，特别是‘d’的定义和其可能导致的错误解的问题。
• [Animats]提到的GJK算法在处理非唯一解和平坦多边形表面时遇到的实际问题和解决方法也引发了对算法健壮性的讨论。

• [Animats] 认为GJK算法在处理凸壳距离问题时需要关注数值误差，特别是在处理非唯一解的情况下，例如立方体放在立方体上时会出现的面对面接触问题。他还提到平坦多边形表面的细分问题会导致算法循环，并指出Stephen Cameron在1990年代的研究解决了部分问题。此外，他提到近似的凸分解算法可以生成更干净的几何形状，但需要从干净的几何开始。
• [ttw44] 表示对独立游戏开发中有关复杂物理引擎的资料稀缺的担忧，认为这些知识往往只在行业内或GitHub上能找到。
• [msteffen] 对数学推导中的两个等价命题感到困惑，特别是关于‘d’的定义和使用，担心如果‘d’过大可能导致错误的解。
• [leoqa] 提到分离轴定理（Sep Axis Theorem）作为一个简单易解释的算法，可以用于面试中解释给非技术人员听，并描述了其在碰撞检测中的应用。
• [reactordev] 关注非球形形状的处理，指出在处理大量顶点时碰撞检测的复杂性，并强调任何减少光线测试或剪裁的优化都是有价值的。

补充讨论：
• [socalgal2] 提供了相关的讨论链接，指向几日前的一个讨论。
• [EGreg] 提到自己在25年前就写过相关主题的文章，并提供了链接。
• [double051] 识别出评论中提到的测试案例是Halo 2中的Ascension。
• [MortyWaves] 抱怨Hacker News上提交的链接常常带有cookie垃圾信息。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在[msteffen]对数学推导的疑问，特别是‘d’的定义和其可能导致的错误解的问题。
• [Animats]提到的GJK算法在处理非唯一解和平坦多边形表面时遇到的实际问题和解决方法也引发了对算法健壮性的讨论。

data.author: ghuntley
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个由GHuntley开发的COBOL项目，包含三种不同的计算器实现：基本计算器、逆波兰表示法（RPN）计算器和使用表情符号运算符的RPN计算器。项目展示了COBOL的现代特性，如表情符号支持和错误处理。

### 主要功能：
1. **基本计算器**：支持四则运算，保护除零错误，交互式循环。
2. **RPN计算器**：基于堆栈的评估，支持复杂表达式和错误处理，附带全面测试套件。
3. **表情符号RPN计算器**：使用表情符号作为运算符，支持Unicode和彩色错误消息，带有成功庆祝标志（🎉）。

### 使用方法：
- 通过命令行编译和运行各个计算器。
- 提供测试套件和测试运行脚本以验证功能。

### 项目结构：
包含多个COBOL文件和Shell脚本，用于实现和测试计算器功能。

### 环境设置：
- macOS上通过Homebrew安装GNU COBOL。
- Linux和Windows也有相应安装指南。

该项目展示了COBOL在现代计算中的应用潜力。

COBOL Calculator Collection 🧮
A collection of calculators written in COBOL, demonstrating different computational paradigms and modern features like emoji support.
Overview
This project contains three different calculator implementations:
Basic Calculator
- Traditional infix notation calculator
RPN Calculator
- Reverse Polish Notation calculator with stack-based evaluation
Emoji RPN Calculator
- Modern RPN calculator using emoji operators (➕➖✖➗)
Prerequisites
macOS Setup
Install GNU COBOL (GnuCOBOL) via Homebrew:
brew install gnu-cobol
This will install:
cobc
- COBOL compiler
Required dependencies (berkeley-db, gmp, json-c)
Other Platforms
Linux
: Install
gnucobol
or
open-cobol
via your package manager
Windows
: Install GnuCOBOL from the official website
Project Structure
.
├── README.md                    # This file
├── calculator.cob               # Basic infix calculator
├── rpn-calculator.cob          # RPN calculator
├── emoji-rpn-calculator.cob    # Emoji RPN calculator
├── test-rpn.cob               # Test suite for RPN calculator
├── test-emoji-rpn.cob         # Test suite for emoji RPN calculator
├── run-tests.sh               # Test runner for RPN calculator
├── run-emoji-tests.sh         # Test runner for emoji calculator
└── emoji-test.cob             # Emoji support verification
Quick Start
1. Basic Calculator
Compile and run the traditional calculator:
cobc -x calculator.cob -o calculator
./calculator
Example usage:
==============================
COBOL CALCULATOR
==============================
Enter first number: 10
Enter operation (+, -, *, /): +
Enter second number: 5
Result: 0000000010.00 + 0000000005.00 = 000000000000015.00
2. RPN Calculator
Compile and run the RPN calculator:
cobc -x rpn-calculator.cob -o rpn-calculator
./rpn-calculator
Example usage:
==============================
RPN COBOL CALCULATOR
==============================
Enter RPN expression (e.g. 3 4 + or 10 2 /):
3 4 +
Result: +0000000007.00
3. Emoji RPN Calculator 🎉
Compile and run the emoji calculator:
cobc -x emoji-rpn-calculator.cob -o emoji-rpn-calculator
./emoji-rpn-calculator
Example usage:
========================================
🧮 EMOJI RPN CALCULATOR 🧮
========================================
Enter RPN expression using emoji operators:
➕ for addition    ➖ for subtraction
✖ for multiply     ➗ for division
Example: 3 4 ➕  or  10 2 ➗
3 4 ➕
Result: +0000000007.00 🎉
Running Tests
RPN Calculator Tests
#
Run test suite directly
cobc -x test-rpn.cob -o test-rpn
./test-rpn
#
Or use the test runner script
chmod +x run-tests.sh
./run-tests.sh
Emoji RPN Calculator Tests
#
Run emoji test suite directly
cobc -x test-emoji-rpn.cob -o test-emoji-rpn
./test-emoji-rpn
#
Or use the emoji test runner script
chmod +x run-emoji-tests.sh
./run-emoji-tests.sh
Features
Basic Calculator
✅ Four basic operations (+, -, *, /)
✅ Decimal number support
✅ Division by zero protection
✅ Interactive loop
RPN Calculator
✅ Stack-based evaluation
✅ Complex expression support
✅ Space-separated input parsing
✅ Error handling for invalid expressions
✅ Comprehensive test suite (20 test cases)
Emoji RPN Calculator
✅ Modern emoji operators (➕➖✖➗)
✅ Unicode support in COBOL
✅ Colorful error messages with emojis
✅ Success celebrations (🎉)
✅ Full test coverage (12 test cases)
RPN Expression Examples
Basic Operations
3 4 ➕       → 7      (3 + 4)
10 3 ➖      → 7      (10 - 3)
4 5 ✖       → 20     (4 * 5)
20 4 ➗      → 5      (20 / 4)
Complex Expressions
15 7 1 1 ➕ ➖ ➗ 3 ✖ 2 1 1 ➕ ➕ ➖  → 5
2 3 ➕ 4 5 ➕ ✖                    → 45  ((2+3) * (4+5))
1 2 ➕ 3 ➕ 4 ➕                    → 10  (((1+2)+3)+4)
Error Handling
Both RPN calculators include comprehensive error handling:
Division by zero
:
Error: Division by zero ➗
Insufficient operands
:
Error: Need 2 operands for ➕
Stack overflow
:
Error: Stack overflow! 💥
Stack underflow
:
Error: Stack underflow! ⚠️
Invalid expressions
:
Error: Invalid RPN expression! ❌
Technical Details
COBOL Features Demonstrated
Data structures
: Stack implementation using OCCURS clause
String handling
: Token parsing and manipulation
Control f

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在不同处理器架构上的代码优化、技术学习经历、具体代码实现的正确性以及文章风格和AI生成内容的争议。

不同观点：
• **代码优化在不同架构上的差异**：_notreallyme_ 指出，在无MMU处理器和现代MMU甚至NUMA能力的处理器上优化代码有很大不同。他认为旧的优化技巧在现代架构上可能变得非常慢，尤其在没有考虑缓存层次和内存管理的情况下。
• **技术学习经历的影响**：martinald 分享了自己在90年代末学习技术的经历，强调了由于经济限制和当时的技术环境，他们需要深入了解许多基础知识来解决问题。这种经历塑造了他们的技术能力。
• **查找表与计算的性能对比**：U1F984 质疑“查找表总是比计算快”的观点，认为由于现代内存速度远慢于CPU，只有在查找表能放入L1缓存的情况下才可能更快。
• **代码实现的正确性**：reidrac 对文章中提到的Z80代码示例提出质疑，认为代码中存在不必要的操作和不合理的选择，比如使用不合适的寄存器和指令。

补充讨论：
• **文章风格和AI生成内容的争议**：orbifold、DrNosferatu 和 faefox 都提到了文章的写作风格，怀疑其可能是由AI生成的。他们认为这种风格干扰了读者的理解和参与。
• **许可证问题**：mdaniel 提醒作者在代码仓库中添加许可证，以避免让读者猜测作者的意图和版权声明。
• **技术内容的准确性**：IceDane 和 peteforde 对文章中提到的“移植SAP”和“用Z80方式编写ABAP”提出了质疑，认为这些说法不准确或者缺乏具体解释。
• **点击诱饵和娱乐性**：renewiltord 认为文章标题有 clickbait 的性质，但同时也承认文章内容有趣，并分享了一个娱乐视频来进一步娱乐读者。

争议焦点：
• **查找表与计算的性能对比**：在现代硬件上，查找表和计算的性能比较存在争议，具体效果依赖于缓存命中和内存访问速度。
• **代码实现的正确性和优化**：Z80代码示例中的具体实现和优化选择引起了讨论，尤其是关于寄存器使用和指令选择的合理性。
• **文章风格和AI生成内容的可信度**：文章是否由AI生成及其对内容理解的影响引发了讨论。

总结：评论主要围绕代码优化、技术学习经历、具体代码实现的正确性以及文章风格和AI生成内容的争议展开，涉及性能优化、技术细节、版权问题和文章娱乐性等多方面的讨论。

data.article_summary: 自20世纪70年代以来，可再生能源故事不断被讲述，但直到最近两年，可再生能源才真正成为全球主流且具成本效益的选择。自1954年发明光伏电池以来，全球安装太阳能的第一个太瓦用时近70年，而第二个太瓦仅用两年，第三个太瓦预计将在今年或明年达成。2022年，96%的新增电力需求由可再生能源满足，美国93%的新增发电能力来自太阳能、风能和储能设备。加州在可再生能源使用上创下纪录，而德州在可再生能源和储能安装方面甚至超过了加州。中国则是全球可再生能源安装和出口的领头羊，其碳排放已开始下降。这一转变为应对气候危机带来了巨大希望。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：可再生能源（尤其是太阳能）的发展现状、优势、挑战及未来前景

不同观点：
• **跨洲电缆传输可再生能源**：[jillesvangurp] 认为，电缆技术（特别是长距离高压直流电缆）可以解决太阳能不稳定的问题。通过跨洲、跨时区的电力传输，可以平衡供需，充分利用各地过剩的太阳能和风能。这一技术目前未被充分使用，但未来有巨大潜力。
  
• **分布式能源与技术跨越**：[ErigmolCt] 指出，像纳米比亚这样的国家正在通过分布式太阳能技术实现跨越式发展，而不是依赖传统的化石能源。这种技术跨越让一些发展中国家能够绕过20世纪的能源发展路径。

• **能源问题解决后的社会形态讨论**：[louwrentius] 引用了《星际迷航》中的概念，提到如果未来能源问题得到彻底解决，社会可能会发生根本性变化，人们可能会失去以利润为导向的生活目标。

• **热泵技术的兴起**：[Animats] 提到热泵销量已经超过传统炉具，表明可再生能源相关技术在成本和效率上的显著进步。

• **太阳能产业的地缘政治问题**：[jonplackett] 质疑太阳能是否真的解决了能源的地缘政治问题，因为中国在太阳能板生产中占据主导地位，可能导致新的权力集中。

• **可再生能源与碳预算**：[Biologist123] 对可再生能源增长是否能赶上碳预算消耗表示担忧，认为这是评估能源转型的关键指标。

• **工程与市场的结合**：[thomascountz] 强调太阳能的经济效益，认为工程进步与市场需求结合是推动其快速发展的关键。

• **托尼·塞巴的预测**：[audunw] 推荐了托尼·塞巴的观点，认为他对能源转型的预测非常准确且鼓舞人心，尽管看似过于乐观。

• **对中国市场主导地位的批评**：[arh5451] 认为文章未充分讨论中国如何通过国家支持手段主导太阳能市场，并指出能源储存技术的重要性。

• **对文章写作风格的批评**：[pzo] 认为文章使用文字而非数字表述数据，增加了阅读难度，建议改进。

补充讨论：
• **对能源转型的情感反应**：[danaris] 对文章的积极和希望的基调表示赞赏，并强调太阳能技术对农业等领域的直接影响，如减少柴油消耗，显著降低农民的成本。

• **对能源转型的批判性思考**：[ambientenv] 对文章的乐观叙述持保留态度，提到需要更批判性地看待能源转型过程中的问题。

• **对太阳能历史性发展的感叹**：[Aardwolf] 幽默地指出，太阳对地球生命的重要性并非新发现，但如今太阳能技术的快速发展确实引人注目。

People have been telling stories about renewable energy since the nineteen-seventies, when the first all-solar-powered house opened on the campus of the University of Delaware, drawing a hundred thousand visitors in 1973, its first year, to marvel at its early photovoltaic panels and its solar hot-water system, complete with salt tubs in the basement to store heat overnight. But, even though we’ve got used to seeing solar panels and wind turbines across the landscape in the intervening fifty years, we continue to think of what they produce as “alternative energy,” a supplement to the fossil-fuelled power that has run Western economies for more than two centuries. In the past two years, however, with surprisingly little notice, renewable energy has suddenly become the obvious, mainstream, cost-efficient choice around the world. Against all the big bad things happening on the planet (and despite all the best efforts of the Republican-led Congress in recent weeks), this is a very big and hopeful thing, which a short catalogue of recent numbers demonstrates:
It took from the invention of the photovoltaic solar cell, in 1954, until 2022 for the world to install a terawatt of solar power; the second terawatt came just two years later, and the third will arrive either later this year or early next.
That’s because people are now putting up a gigawatt’s worth of solar panels, the rough equivalent of the power generated by one coal-fired plant, every fifteen hours. Solar power is now growing faster than any power source in history, and it is closely followed by wind power—which is really another form of energy from the sun, since it is differential heating of the earth that produces the wind that turns the turbines.
Last year, ninety-six per cent of the global demand for new electricity was met by renewables, and in the United States ninety-three per cent of new generating capacity came from solar, wind, and an ever-increasing variety of batteries to store that power.
In March, for the first time, fossil fuels generated less than half the electricity in the U.S. In California, at one point on May 25th, renewables were producing a record hundred and fifty-eight per cent of the state’s power demand. Over the course of the entire day, they produced eighty-two per cent of
the power in California
, which, this spring, surpassed Japan to become the world’s fourth-largest economy.
Meanwhile, battery-storage capability has increased seventy-six per cent, based on this year’s projected estimates; at night, those batteries are often the main supplier of California’s electricity. As the director of reliability analysis at the North American Electric Reliability Corporation put it, in the
CleanTechnica
newsletter, “batteries can smooth out some of that variability from those times when the wind isn’t blowing or the sun isn’t shining.” As a result, California is so far using forty per cent less natural gas to generate electricity than it did in 2023, which is the single most hopeful statistic I’ve seen in four decades of writing about the climate crisis.
Texas is now installing renewable energy and batteries faster than California; in a single week in March, it set records for solar and wind production as well as for battery discharge. In May, when the state was hit by a near-record-breaking early-season heat wave, air-conditioners helped create a record demand on the grid, which didn’t blink—more than a quarter of the power came from the sun and wind. Last week’s flooding tragedy was a reminder of how vulnerable the state is to extreme weather, especially as water temperatures rise in the Gulf, producing more moisture in the air; in late June, the director of the state’s utility system said that the chances of emergency outages had dropped from sixteen per cent last summer to less than one per cent this year, mostly because the state had added ten thousand megawatts of solar power and battery storage. That, he said, “puts us in a better position.”
All this is dwarfed by what’s happening in China, which currently installs more than half the world’s renewable energy and storage within its own borders, and exports most of the solar panels and batteries used by the rest of the world. In May, according to government records, China had installed a record ninety-three gigawatts of solar power—amounting to a gigawatt every eight hours. The pace was apparently paying off—analysts reported that, in the first quarter of the year, total carbon emissions in China had actually decreased; emissions linked to producing electricity fell nearly six per cent, as solar and wind have replaced coal. In 2024, almost half the automobiles sold in China, which is the world’s largest car market, were full or hybrid electric vehicles. data.title: Evolution Mail Users Easily Trackable
data.author: mike-cardwell
data.article_summary: Evolution Mail的“加载远程内容”隐私保护功能失效多年未修复。即使该选项关闭，含有特定HTML标签的邮件仍会触发DNS请求或建立连接，泄露用户是否阅读邮件及其大致位置。开发团队将问题归咎于WebKitGTK，且未有近期修复计划。作者建议，若重视隐私，应卸载Evolution Mail，因其无法保护用户隐私，且开发者不认为这是他们的责任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HTML邮件及其相关的隐私与安全问题

不同观点：
• [akimbostrawman] 认为HTML邮件一直是个错误，暗示其设计不合理。
• [aitacobell] 指出，有缺陷的隐私功能比没有隐私功能更糟糕，暗示不完善的功能可能带来更多问题。
• [ajross] 强烈批评HTML作为邮件格式的复杂性和安全隐患，认为其导致了邮件使用的减少，并指出邮件客户端缺乏浏览器那样的标准遵从和安全措施。

补充讨论：
• [dvdkon] 提到WebKit漏洞报告有最新活动，表示对问题解决持乐观态度，提供了一个具体的参考链接。
• [NoahZuniga] 关心Thunderbird是否能防御这种跟踪方式，提出了对具体邮件客户端防护能力的疑问。
• [gucci-on-fleek] 分享了Evolution邮件客户端的设置技巧，可以通过默认使用纯文本版本来减少HTML邮件的影响，提供了具体操作步骤。
• [btown] 讨论了HTML邮件预处理的防御策略，建议通过白名单方式过滤HTML标签和属性，并询问是否有优秀的HTML预处理工具。
• [kosolam] 指出即使关闭图片加载，Gmail也会向跟踪服务泄露邮件打开信息，强调了更深层次的隐私泄露问题。
• [monster_truck] 仅对术语“whitelist”进行了更正，未深入讨论技术问题。
• [InvisGhost] 认为开发者未能重视问题，Evolution需要进行公关损害控制，并讨论了开发者应如何应对和改变以避免未来问题。
• [arp242] 对DNS日志和SNI头信息泄露的实际风险持怀疑态度，认为虽然存在问题，但其实际影响有限，并为WebKitGTK的处理方式辩护。

争议焦点：
• HTML邮件格式及其带来的隐私和安全问题是否严重，以及邮件客户端应如何有效防御这些风险。
• 开发者是否足够重视和及时修复相关漏洞，用户对邮件客户端防护能力的期望与现实之间的差距。

44512684.article_content:
Evolution Mail Users Easily Trackable
Written an hour ago by Mike Cardwell
Evolution Mail’s “Load Remote Content” option, as a privacy protection feature doesn’t work. They know it doesn’t work. It hasn’t worked for years and there is no sign it will be fixed any time soon.
I discovered the other day that if a HTML email contains a tag like:
<link
rel
=
"dns-prefetch"
href
=
"https://trackingcode.attackersdomain.example.com"
>
Then when an email is opened in Evolution Mail, a DNS request for trackingcode.attackersdomain.example.com is performed. This happens with remote content disabled, and without clicking the button to fetch it. The sender can look at their DNS logs to see if you’ve read your email, and the IP address of your DNS resolver at that time, which may indicate your location.
I opened a
bug report
with Evolution Mail, and they blamed WebKitGTK for this situation and have closed my ticket as a
duplicate of another ticket
which was opened in April 2024. That ticket reported a different but similar bug:
<link
href
=
"trackingcode.attackersdomain.example.com"
rel
=
"preconnect"
>
This apparently triggers a connection when you read an email, even without clicking to load remote content. An attacker could look at the SNI header during the TLS negotiation to identify the unique reader of such an email, and it would grant them their IP address.
This one
links back to a webkit bug
which was opened in August 2023, which also suggests there will be other such leaks, and which shows no sign of being dealt with.
I suggested that maintaining a whitelist of allowed html tags and attributes, and stripping them before passing the email html onto a web browser would be a good defense in depth strategy, but this looks unlikely to be followed.
So my suggestion is: If you care about having privacy when reading your email, uninstall Evolution Mail. It doesn’t protect your privacy, and the devs don’t consider that to be their responsibility.
Want to leave a tip?
You can follow this Blog using
RSS
or
Mastodon
. To read more, visit my
blog index
.

data.title: Archaeologists unveil 3,500-year-old city in Peru
data.author: neversaydie
data.article_summary: 考古学家在秘鲁北部巴兰卡省发现了一座距今3500年的古城佩尼科（Peñico），该城建于公元前1800至1500年之间，位于海拔600米的山坡上，距利马北部约200公里。佩尼科被认为是连接太平洋沿岸社区与安第斯山脉和亚马逊盆地居民的重要贸易枢纽。研究显示，该城有18座建筑，包括仪式庙宇和住宅建筑，出土文物包括仪式物品、陶土雕塑和贝壳项链。佩尼科靠近公元前3000年建立的卡拉尔文明，这一发现有助于理解卡拉尔文明在气候变化影响后的发展。考古学家Ruth Shady指出，佩尼科在贸易和文化交流中占据战略位置，是卡拉尔社会的延续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于秘鲁Peñico古城的发现及其历史意义的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [ErigmolCt] 认为Peñico古城的发现显示了秘鲁古代文明在贸易、建筑和艺术方面的独立发展，与同时期的美索不达米亚和埃及文明相媲美。这强调了古代文明在全球不同地区的多样性和独立性。

• [slimebot80] 对考古工作的时间跨度提出疑问，质疑为何经过8年的发掘工作，遗迹在照片中看起来如此明显，而8年前却完全被埋没。这暗示了对考古工作进度和公布结果的怀疑。

Archaeologists have announced the discovery of an ancient city in Peru's northern Barranca province.
The 3,500-year-old city, named PeÃ±ico, is believed to have served as a key trading hub connecting early Pacific coast communities with those living in the Andes mountains and Amazon basin.
Located some 200km north of Lima, the site lies about 600 metres (1,970 feet) above sea level and is thought to have been founded between 1,800 and 1,500 BC - around the same time that early civilisations were flourishing in the Middle East and Asia.
Researchers say the discovery sheds light on what became of the Americas' oldest civilisation, the Caral.
Image source,
Reuters
Image caption,
An aerial view of the archaeological zone of PeÃ±ico, in Peru, an ancient city established 3,500 years ago
Drone footage released by researchers shows a circular structure on a hillside terrace at the city's centre, surrounded by the remains of stone and mud buildings.
Eight years of research at the site unearthed 18 structures, including ceremonial temples and residential complexes.
In buildings at the site, researchers discovered ceremonial objects, clay sculptures of human and animal figures and necklaces made from beads and seashells.
PeÃ±ico is situated close to where Caral, recognised as the oldest known civilisation in the Americas, was established 5,000 years ago at around 3,000 BC in the Supe valley of Peru.
Caral features 32 monuments, including large pyramid structures, sophisticated irrigation agriculture and urban settlements. It is believed to have developed in isolation to other comparative early civilisations in India, Egypt, Sumeria and China.
Dr Ruth Shady, the archaeologist who led the recent research into PeÃ±ico and the excavation of Caral in the 1990s, said that the discovery was important for understanding what became of the Caral civilisation after it was decimated by climate change.
The PeÃ±ico community was "situated in a strategic location for trade, for exchange with societies from the coast, the highlands and the jungle", Dr Shady told the Reuters news agency.
At a news conference unveiling the findings on Thursday, archaeologist Marco Machacuay, a researcher with the Ministry of Culture, said that PeÃ±ico's significance lies in it being a continuation of the Caral society.
Peru is home to many of the Americas' most significant archaeological discoveries, including the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu in the Andes and the mysterious Nazca Lines etched into the desert along the central coast.

data.title: Show HN: FlopperZiro – A DIY open-source Flipper Zero clone
data.author: iraton
data.article_summary: FlopperZiro是一个开源、低成本、可自行DIY的Flipper Zero克隆项目，使用Arduino IDE进行编程。项目硬件包括STM32微控制器、RF收发模块、PN532/PN7150 RFID/NFC模块、OLED显示屏、红外收发器等组件。它支持RubberDucky、RFID/NFC、IR、RF等功能，可通过SD卡保存/加载数据，并显示电池及存储剩余百分比。软件方面仍在开发中，包括解决SD卡和显示问题、完善菜单及功能。项目提供3D打印外壳设计，硬件PCB也在持续改进。FlopperZiro是一个趣味项目，不具备专业设备的功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LilyGo T-Embed CC1100与FlipperZero的比较及其替代品

不同观点：
• [boznz] 认为LilyGo T-Embed CC1100在硬件上与FlipperZero类似，且具有WiFi/Bluetooth功能，运行Bruce Pentest固件，价格不到FlipperZero的一半。虽然Bruce固件不如FlipperZero的精致，但其硬件和软件都是开源且易于修改的。
• [Chihuahua0633] 提出LilyGo和Capibara Zero等设备是否具有与FlipperZero相同的软件支持，并指出FlipperZero强大的社区支持是其受欢迎的重要因素。
• [Neywiny] 强调LilyGo T-Embed CC1100的RF功能有限，主要是一个433 MHz的重放攻击设备，功能相对简单，避免对其有过高期望。
• [voidUpdate] 关心设备是否检查频率许可要求。
• [conradev] 提出是否可以用现代智能手机为这些设备供电，并提到Flipper Zero的体积和充电问题。

补充讨论：
• [net01] 提到类似项目Kiisu V4A，可以运行Flipper代码和修改后的Flipper代码。
• [s-mon] 开玩笑说在Defcon的拉斯维加斯酒店可能会对这种设备感到惊讶。
• [aitacobell] 幽默地指出设备是否像Tamagotchi。
• [kevo1ution] 对NFC支持感到兴奋。
• [macawfish] 喜欢设备的名字。
• [vsviridov] 开玩笑地问什么时候会有FlopperOne。
• [karolist] 提供Capibara Zero的链接作为替代品。
• [anfractuosity] 询问是否有人见过AliExpress上的Flipper Zero克隆品。
• [zeroq] 指出Flipper Zero的吸引力部分在于其社交媒体曝光率和名人效应，可以带来额外的关注。

争议焦点：
• 设备的功能和软件支持：LilyGo T-Embed CC1100与FlipperZero在功能和软件支持上的比较，尤其是社区支持和开源性。
• 设备的RF能力：LilyGo T-Embed CC1100的RF功能是否如宣传的那样强大，还是相对简单。
• 设备的实用性和便携性：设备供电和便携性的讨论，尤其是与现代智能手机结合使用的可能性。

data.title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
data.author: GavCo
data.article_summary: Biomni是一款通用的生物医学AI代理，旨在自动执行各种生物医学研究任务，通过整合大型语言模型（LLM）推理、检索增强规划和基于代码的执行，帮助科学家大幅提高研究效率并生成可测试的假设。用户可以通过设置脚本安装Biomni，并使用自然语言执行如CRISPR筛选、单细胞RNA测序注释和化合物ADMET性质预测等任务。Biomni是一个开放科学项目，鼓励社区贡献新工具、数据集、软件和基准等。当前正开发下一代版本Biomni-E2，贡献者将有机会在顶级期刊上共同署名发表论文。Biomni基于Apache-2.0许可证发布，但某些集成工具可能有更严格的商业许可证。更多信息和使用方法可访问biomni.stanford.edu。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个具有特定工具集和Python执行功能的智能代理系统在生物医学研究中的应用和潜力

不同观点：
• deepdarkforest：认为该系统通过预设的工具集和Python执行功能，能够有效缩小错误范围，尤其在处理标准化数据时具有优势。但也指出实际数据往往更复杂，工具的长期优势有待观察，特别是在处理专有数据集时。
• Edmond：看好该系统在科学研究中的潜力，并提到可能用于构建智能工作空间以辅助科研。
• andy99：关注该系统在生物威胁评估方面的风险，虽然对当前LLM的能力持怀疑态度，但认为该方向值得关注。
• joelthelion：质疑该系统在实际工作中的有效性和实用性，希望有业内人士提供意见。
• freedomben：对AI在医学研究和药物开发中的应用充满期待，认为AI在数据模式识别方面具有巨大潜力。
• teenvan_1995：对提供150多个工具的数量表示担忧，认为需要在实际应用中验证其有效性。
• dbcooper：询问是否有邀请名额，显示出对系统访问的兴趣。
• epistasis：对能够尝试该系统感到兴奋，表明其对该技术的前景看好。
• dmezzetti：分享了与生物医学文献分析相关的开源项目，提供了额外的技术资源和工具链接。
• AIorNot：将该系统推荐给在Crispr实验室工作的朋友，显示出对该系统实际应用的认可。
• SalmoShalazar：认为当前类似软件的泛滥表明创新有限，主要是围绕特定领域对LLM进行专业化包装，创新性不足。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：该系统在实际应用中的有效性和长期优势，特别是在处理复杂和专有数据集时的表现。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是该系统在生物威胁评估方面的潜在风险及其对科学研究的影响。
• 用户对工具数量和实际应用中的可行性表示关注，认为需要更多实际验证。
• 部分用户对AI在科学研究中的创新性和应用前景充满期待，并分享了相关资源和项目。

Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
Overview
Biomni is a general-purpose biomedical AI agent designed to autonomously execute a wide range of research tasks across diverse biomedical subfields. By integrating cutting-edge large language model (LLM) reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, Biomni helps scientists dramatically enhance research productivity and generate testable hypotheses.
Quick Start
Installation
Our software environment is massive and we provide a single setup.sh script to setup.
Follow this
file
to setup the env first.
Then activate the environment E1:
conda activate biomni_e1
then install the latest biomni package:
pip install biomni --upgrade
Or install from the github source version.
Lastly, configure your API keys in bash profile
~/.bashrc
:
export

YOUR_API_KEY
"
export

"
YOUR_API_KEY
"

optional if you just use Claude

data.title: The jank programming language
data.author: akkad33
data.article_summary: Jank是一种通用的编程语言，兼容Clojure，但通过C++和LLVM-based JIT实现，支持原生编译和最小运行时。它提供REPL开发环境，同时能够进行静态AOT编译生成原生可执行文件。Jank允许在Clojure代码中无缝嵌入C++代码，并支持多线程软件事务内存和反应代理系统。其编译器启动快、内存使用低，并提供高质量的错误报告。Jank还与Clojure生态工具（如Leiningen和nREPL）兼容，支持在同一文件中混合编写C++和Clojure代码。例子展示了如何利用Clojure强大的数据处理能力生成电影索引和转换字节大小为可读格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新语言Jank的开发、设计选择、名称、工具及其与Clojure的关系等的讨论。

不同观点：
• Jeaye（Jank的创建者）认为Jank通过LLVM和C++互操作性实现了独特的功能，如JIT编译和无缝的C++集成，且保留了Clojure的核心特性如nREPL。他计划在年底发布第一个alpha版本，并定期更新开发进展。
• Densh基于其在Scala Native上的经验，提出几点建议：避免提供向后兼容的JVM API子集，避免自己实现GC而是使用mmtk，重视多线程和并发，以及不过度优化单线程性能。
• Catfacts提到另一个类似的项目Clapp（Common Lisp在C++中使用LLVM），并指出Clapp的进展缓慢和编译时间长的问题。他对Jank能否避免类似问题表示关注，并建议从其他类似项目如ECL和Julia中吸取经验。
• Lisbbb对如何通过这些小众语言谋生表示疑问，回忆起Clojure在过去十几年的低迷，并对2025年还能看到Clojure或LISP的复兴表示惊讶。
• Mgdev表达了对项目的喜爱，但建议更改名称，以避免因名称问题在工作中受到限制。
• Norir建议采用一个更小的自举子集来简化设计，并通过C编译器和共享库实现REPL功能，认为当前的设计可能会导致不必要的复杂性。
• Lewdwig对Clojure曾经的辉煌和后来的停滞表示感慨，并希望Jank能为其带来新的活力。
• Jhoechtl提到与Janet语言的相关性。
• Padjo对Jank作为一个真实语言而不是一个深奥或玩笑语言表示惊讶。
• Lyngbakr关注Jank的工具链，希望其工具能像Gleam一样开箱即用。
• Defo10对Jank的错误报告功能表示期待，并希望看到与JVM的性能对比基准。
• Sideeffffect关心跨平台的Clojure库是否能在Jank中直接使用，以及需要做的调整。
• Jankjankjank幽默地表示感觉自己已经在写Jank代码了。
• Axblount质疑除了缺少JVM外，还有什么因素阻碍Jank成为Clojure的替代品。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Jank是否应该提供向后兼容的JVM API子集，以及如何平衡新功能和复杂性。
• 另一个关注点是编译时间和性能优化，特别是与Clapp等类似项目的比较。
• 多线程和并发支持被认为是设计初期需要重视的问题，以避免后期改造的困难。
• 工具链和错误报告功能也被多次提及，显示出社区对这些方面的重视。
• 名称问题虽然是一个小问题，但在实际应用中可能会影响项目的接受度。

44482273.article_content:
jank programming language - Clojure/LLVM/C++
The jank programming language
jank is a
general-purpose programming language
which embraces the
interactive, value-oriented
nature of Clojure as well as the desire for
native compilation and minimal runtimes
. jank is
strongly compatible with Clojure
and considers itself a dialect of Clojure. Please note that jank is under heavy development; assume all features are planned or incomplete.
Where jank differs from Clojure JVM is that its host is C++ on top of an
LLVM-based JIT
. This allows jank to offer the same benefits of
REPL-based development
while being able to
seamlessly reach into the native world
and compete seriously with JVM's performance.
Still, jank is a Clojure dialect and thus includes its
code-as-data philosophy and powerful macro system
. jank remains a functional-first language which builds upon Clojure's rich set of
persistent, immutable data structures
. When mutability is needed, jank offers a software transaction memory and reactive agent system to ensure
clean and correct multi-threaded designs
.
Current progress
Github
Sponsor
Wide spectrum dynamics
Enjoy both REPL iteration with JIT compilation and static AOT compilation to native executables.
01
Iterate like you would with Clojure
Iterate in the REPL and build your program from the ground up without leaving your editor.
(
defn
-main
[
& args
]
(
loop
[
game-state
(
new-game!
)]
(
when
(
done?
game-state
)
(
end-game!
game-state
)
(
recur
(
next-state
game-state
)))))
02
Reach into the native world
Seamlessly switch to inline C++ within your Clojure source, while still having access to your Clojure code using interpolation.
(
defn
create-vertex-shader!
[]
(
c++/glCreateShader
c++/GL_VERTEX_SHADER
))
(

[
shader source
]
(
let
[
shader
(
int
shader
)
source
(
str
source
)]
(
c++/glShaderSource
shader
1
source c++/nullptr
)))
(
defn
compile-shader!
[
shader
]
(
c++/glCompileShader
(
int
shader
)))
03
Compile to machine code
jank is built on an LLVM-based JIT. With AOT enabled, both statically and dynamically linked executables can be generated. The jank compiler itself has very speedy start times and low memory usage.
$
time
taskset
0x1
clj
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m1.127s
user
0m0.997s
sys
0m0.111s
$
time
taskset
0x1
jank
run
hello-world.clj
hello
world
real
0m0.086s
user
0m0.045s
sys
0m0.040s
04
World-class errors
jank stands in its own category among lisps for its error reporting quality. No bloated JVM stack traces, opaque errors, or lack of context.
jank builds upon Clojure.
Keep your existing code; gain more confidence and more speed.
Strongly compatible with Clojure
If it works with Clojure JVM and it works with ClojureScript, it should work with jank. There's a
:jank
reader conditional for when you need it.
REPL and native JIT
Use your favorite nREPL editor plugin. jank uses an LLVM-based JIT to compile machine code on the fly.
Go native
Reach into native libraries or interact directly with your native code base. Seamlessly write both C++ and Clojure in the same file.
Tooling friendly
Leiningen, LSP, nREPL planned from the start. jank's compiler is also written with tooling in mind, so it can be used for lexing, parsing, and analysis.

data.title: Configuring Split Horizon DNS with Pi-Hole and Tailscale
data.author: gm678
data.article_summary:
作者过去使用OpenVPN，但后来转向了基于Wireguard协议的Tailscale，因为它速度更快。Tailscale是加拿大公司，无法查看连接内容，用户也可自行托管。作者设置了Tailscale网络（tailnet），但未配置分离DNS。最初，反向代理服务器被配置为向其局域网IP发送路由。本文介绍了如何配置Pi-hole实现分离DNS：让tailnet客户端获取tailnet IP，局域网客户端获取局域网IP。

某些服务（如Nextcloud）客户端不支持额外认证，导致反向代理配置问题。作者曾通过地理封锁减少攻击面，但这限制了连接灵活性。通过在tailnet上实现分离DNS，可以避免这些问题，并有可能关闭广域网（WAN）访问，强制通过局域网或tailnet访问服务。

Pi-hole利用dnsmasq的分支pihole-FTL实现此功能，根据查询接口返回相应IP地址。这使得不同网络的客户端能获取适合其网络的地址。目前此功能仅支持IPv4。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过自建DNS和VPN等工具实现家庭网络安全与服务暴露的方案讨论

不同观点：
• JoshWVS认为使用dnsmasq和Tailscale的组合是一种有效的解决方案，并分享了自己通过Tailscale的"Funnel"功能将单一服务暴露到互联网的经验，例如自托管Plausible。他还提供了相关博客链接供参考。
• dolmen指出Tailscale的隐私政策发生了变化，特别是对于2024年9月3日之后的新客户账户，将受到美国特拉华州的法律约束，这可能引起对隐私的担忧。他还提到自托管Headscale作为替代方案。
• elashri描述了自己通过Adguard Home和unbound配置DNS的实践，并提到通过Github获取和合并阻止DoH（DNS over HTTPS）地址的列表，虽然不是万无一失，但在家用网络环境下已经足够。
• leipert对Chromecast忽略本地DNS的问题表示不满，并建议将流量强制重定向到本地DNS服务器（如PiHole），但未详细说明具体实现方法。
• snvzz主张通过headscale和VPN加密所有流量，甚至在局域网内也如此，以确保所有通信都是加密的，减少对明文协议的担忧。
• udev4096提出安全问题，询问是否可能通过IP欺骗和SSRF攻击绕过nginx的"allow"配置，但未得到具体解答。

44512470.article_content:
I've long had some form of VPN for my devices to use when I'm out and about.
Although I used to
run OpenVPN
, I moved to
Tailscale
a little while back. Tailscale builds a mesh network using
Wireguard
protocol and so is able to connect and run quite a bit faster than OpenVPN.
Side note: for those wondering, Tailscale is
Canadian
and can't see the content of connections (although if you're worried about this it's also possible to self-host using
Headscale
).
Although the tailnet has been up for some time, I hadn't got around to setting up split horizon DNS for clients on the tailnet. I was in a bit of a hurry when first setting up and so configured my reverse proxy box to advertise a route to it's own LAN IP.
This post talks about configuring my
Pi-hole
to implement a split horizon: returning the tailnet IP to tailnet clients and the LAN IP to LAN clients.
Splitting my Split Horizon
Many of the DNS names that I wanted to do this for
already
had a split horizon:
Clients on both the LAN and the wider internet connect to the same reverse proxy in my DMZ, but LAN clients connect using the proxy's local IP.
The reverse proxy fronts multiple services, most of which have authentication built in. However, it also requires that outside connections pass a separate (and valid) set of authentication credentials before it'll pass their connection on.
Having to authenticate twice is a little annoying though, and the split horizon makes it easy to disable the additional authentication when LAN clients connect:
satisfy any;
allow 192.168.3.0/24;
deny all;
auth_basic "Authenticate you must";
auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/wanaccess.htpasswd;
This extra authentication means that I'm not exposing any element of the backing service's authentication stack to the outside world. The underlying idea is that it
shouldn't matter
that there's an auth bypass zero day in (say) Grafana, because the wider world needs to get past my auth prompt before they can try to detect or exploit it.
You've Got Access: Why Make The Tailnet Special?
Given that there's an ability to access services via the WAN, you might be wondering why it is that I felt that I needed to do something specifically for the tailnet.
Unfortunately, the proxy
can't
enforce additional authentication for some services because those services clients don't support it.
Nextcloud
is a great example of this: the Nextcloud Desktop sync client authenticates with Nextcloud, but
It uses the
Authorization
header to present it's bearer token, so the reverse proxy will see an unexpected (and, to it, invalid) set of credentials
The client doesn't expose a way to add custom headers to the requests that it makes, so I can't simply send a shared secret and have the proxy check a different header
Having the reverse proxy require additional auth breaks off-net Nextcloud clients (and Nextcloud isn't the only service with this issue).
Geoblocking
Originally, I left the affected services accessible to the world.
Unfortunately, I
sometimes
seem to upset people enough to trigger prolonged attempts at compromising my services.
After
one such attempt
, I decided to reduce attack surface by
adding geo-blocking to my reverse proxy
, essentially restricting access to areas that I thought we'd be likely to connect from (or
at least
appear to).
This, of course, comes at a cost in flexibility, with access failing if any of the following are true:
We connected from an IP that doesn't have a location in the GeoDB (or is mislocated)
The ISP that we're connecting from does funky routing stuff and/or uses CGNAT
We've travelled somewhere that we wouldn't normally
Adding split horizon DNS to the tailnet allows me to avoid these scenarios, because the tailnet subnet can be special cased in
exactly
the same way that the LAN is.
It also increases the likelihood that I can close WAN access off and require that a client be on either the LAN or tailnet.
The Plan
The idea was that a tailnet client would also speak to the Pi-hole, but that names would resolve to a tailnet IP:
This is possible because Pi-hole is underpinned by a fork of
dnsmasq
called
pihole-FTL
which has inherited the setting
localise-queries
(in Pi-hole, this is enabled by default).
The
man page for dnsmasq
describes the setting as follows (line breaks mine):
Return answers to DNS queries from /etc/hosts and
--interface-name
and
--dynamic-host
which depend on the interface over which the query was received.
If a name has more than one address associated with it, and at least one of those addresses is on the same subnet as the interface to which the query was sent, then return only the address(es) on that subnet and return all the available addresses otherwise.
This allows for a server to have multiple addresses in /etc/hosts corresponding to each of its interfaces, and hosts will get the correct address based on which network they are attached to.
Currently this facility is limited to IPv4.
This means that we can create the following record set in
/etc/
44512470.article_summary:
作者过去使用OpenVPN，但后来转向了基于Wireguard协议的Tailscale，因为它速度更快。Tailscale是加拿大公司，无法查看连接内容，用户也可自行托管。作者设置了Tailscale网络（tailnet），但未配置分离DNS。最初，反向代理服务器被配置为向其局域网IP发送路由。本文介绍了如何配置Pi-hole实现分离DNS：让tailnet客户端获取tailnet IP，局域网客户端获取局域网IP。

某些服务（如Nextcloud）客户端不支持额外认证，导致反向代理配置问题。作者曾通过地理封锁减少攻击面，但这限制了连接灵活性。通过在tailnet上实现分离DNS，可以避免这些问题，并有可能关闭广域网（WAN）访问，强制通过局域网或tailnet访问服务。

Pi-hole利用dnsmasq的分支pihole-FTL实现此功能，根据查询接口返回相应IP地址。这使得不同网络的客户端能获取适合其网络的地址。目前此功能仅支持IPv4。

data.title: Nuclear Waste Reprocessing Gains Momentum in the U.S.
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 美国正致力于解决核废料问题。法国Orano公司在拉黑格的设施展示了通过先进技术回收和处理用过的核燃料，特别是将持久性强的放射性污泥转化为更稳定、危害较小的物质。这种方法不仅减少了核废料的体积，还降低了其长期放射性风险。研究人员利用创新化学工艺处理这些废物，目标是提高核能的可持续性和安全性，为应对气候变化提供更环保的能源选择。这一进展对全球核废料管理具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：核燃料循环与核废料处理的技术与经济性

不同观点：
• philipkglass认为，将核废料中的钚回收制成混合氧化物（MOX）燃料在经济上不具吸引力。美国的MOX项目因成本和进度问题被取消，且天然铀价格不高，分离钚并不能显著节省废料处理成本。同时提到激光 enrichment 技术作为另一种回收方法。
• chickenbig质疑相关文章缺乏具体数据，尤其是法国在钚回收和MOX燃料生产上的成本。此外，指出文章混淆了长寿命放射性物质和短寿命裂变产物，强调了分离不同半衰期物质对于废物处理的重要性。
• wffurr以讽刺语气回应，引用文章讨论了核燃料回收的危害，暗示对该技术的担忧。
• vavooom提到锶-90的利用价值，指出其在医学和工程中的应用，显示出对核废料中有价值同位素回收的兴趣。
• greenavocado提出通过结合钍-232和钚燃烧的燃料循环，特别是液态氟化钍反应堆（LFTRs），可以有效解决核废料问题，强调在线后处理技术的重要性。
• mikewarot提到伊利诺伊州Dresden的一个未完成设施，该设施用于存储和处理来自多个反应堆的乏燃料。
• yk对文章中混淆嬗变和后处理的概念表示困惑，指出需要明确区分这两种技术。
• epistasis对当前核能技术的热情表示不解，认为核能技术成熟但成本高昂，缺乏像太阳能和储能技术那样的突破性进展。
• Synaesthesia询问钍反应堆是否能解决核废料处理问题。
• lucidguppy对比核能与太阳能和电池储能，认为后者更能解决问题。
• FilosofumRex提到特朗普政府在民用核能国际协议上的政策，暗示对国际政治影响的关注。
• mathgradthrow对中子束技术表示疑问。
• eagerpace认为可以将核废料储存直到新技术出现，甚至考虑在月球轨道上储存的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体技术包括MOX燃料、激光 enrichment、钍反应堆和LFTRs等。
• 争议焦点包括核废料处理的经济性和技术可行性，特别是后处理和嬗变技术的实际效果和成本。
• 对未来技术突破的期望与当前技术成熟度之间的矛盾也是讨论的重要方面。

data.title: Desktop Publishing Tools That Didn't Make It (2022)
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
本文回顾了20世纪80年代桌面出版软件的早期创新，重点介绍了10款可能被遗忘的软件。桌面出版曾在印刷行业引发革命，尽管随着印刷媒介的衰落，它显得有些过时，但每天仍有大量内容被排版。许多早期工具未能存活至今，包括一些具有开创性但未成功的平台和软件。

1. **Xerox Alto**：虽然严格来说不是专门的桌面出版平台，但其图形用户界面和排版功能启发了后来的Macintosh和桌面出版概念。
2. **The Book Machine**：基于Sirius微型计算机，专为排版设计，但价格昂贵，目标客户是专业技术作者，最终未广泛普及。
3. **MacPublisher**：在PageMaker之前推出，是Mac上早期的桌面出版工具，但不如后者成熟和知名。

这些早期工具展示了桌面出版的演变，尽管许多未能成功，但它们为现代出版技术奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：桌面排版软件（DTP）的发展、现状以及在不同平台上的使用体验，尤其是开源和自由软件的现状与替代方案。

不同观点：
• **[specproc]** 认为从专有软件（如Affinity）切换到Linux平台后，缺乏与Affinity同等级的开源桌面排版软件，尽管可以通过Wine运行一些软件，但更希望找到原生的解决方案。
• **[taeric]** 提到了对《The Print Shop》这一老牌DTP软件的怀旧情感，并分享了一篇相关文章链接，但没有深入讨论软件替代问题。
• **[WillAdams]** 补充了几款未被提及但具有一定影响力的DTP工具，如Calamus、Ready-Set-Go和Microsoft Publisher，并指出某些软件的演变过程，如PageMaker演变为InDesign。
• **[kstrauser]** 分享了自己在高中时使用PageSetter的经历，强调了早期DTP软件对普通用户的革命性影响，尽管技术上有不稳定之处。
• **[jamesgill]** 强调了PageMaker在20世纪80-90年代的广泛流行，并提到自己也曾使用过GeoPublish，特别是在Commodore平台上。
• **[wduquette]** 详细介绍了Victor 9000（在欧洲称为Sirius）这款早期计算机的硬件特性及其在DTP方面的应用，同时分析了其市场失败的原因。
• **[egypturnash]** 指出《The Newsroom》软件的跨平台特性（Apple II、MS-DOS、C64、Atari），并分享了自己使用《The Print Shop》制作个性化图像的怀旧体验。
• **[Brajeshwar]** 认为Aldus PageMaker并未失败，并分享了自己使用PageMaker和CorelDRAW完成学业和工作的经历，同时提到与QuarkXPress的竞争。
• **[cormullion]** 提到了Interleaf这款软件的兴衰，特别是其用Common Lisp编写用户界面的独特性。
• **[leakycap]** 提到了一款基于Apple QuickDraw GX引擎的DTP软件UniQorn，并指出其部分技术在后来的Softpress Freeway网页设计软件中得到了延续。
• **[xp84]** 提到了Letraset的ReadySetGo软件，并分享了自己家庭经营小镇报纸时使用MacWrite和ImageWriter的经历。
• **[paradox460]** 补充了Lighthouse Designs软件和STONEworks在NeXT和早期Mac OS X平台上的重要性，并提到Diagram!演变为如今的OmniGraffle。
• **[ornel]** 分享了20世纪80年代使用Ventura Publisher、Corel Paint和GEM的经历，强调了当时的技术局限和使用体验。
• **[asplake]** 惊讶地发现FrameMaker仍然存在，并提到其过去的使用经历，但未详细说明当前使用情况。
• **[pstuart]** 提到了Quark XPress、Ventura Publisher和PageMaker在DTP领域的应用，并幽默地提到自己通过这些工具练就了出色的排版技能，如在线字距测试。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到不同DTP软件的历史演变和市场竞争，如PageMaker、QuarkXPress和InDesign。
- 怀旧情感贯穿多个评论，尤其是对早期DTP软件如《The Print Shop》和PageSetter的回忆。
- 争议的焦点之一是某些软件是否失败，如[Brajeshwar]对Aldus PageMaker的评价与主流观点相左。
- 对开源和自由软件替代方案的需求和现状也有一定讨论，特别是[specproc]提出的问题。

Today in Tedium:
It’s easy to forget now, but desktop publishing was an immensely innovative thing when it emerged within the computing industry in the early ’80s. While at its heart a mishmash of hardware and software cleverly combined for a single goal, it was an empire builder, one that helped create new businesses and improve the status and positioning of existing ones. And with the decline of print as a medium, it can feel kind of old hat, but lots of stuff still gets typeset every single day. And while we’ve landed on a few standards, a lot of desktop publishing tools failed to make to it the present day. So in a continuation of our list of
things that didn’t make it
, Today’s Tedium takes a look at 10 early examples of desktop publishing software that you probably don’t remember desktop publishing was a killer app nearly 40 years ago and you were in diapers back then … if you existed at all. (Oh yeah,
quick reminder
of what makes things obscure, from our point of view.)

1. Xerox Alto
Platform:
Groundbreaking-but-failed computer platform that inspired the GUI-based world in which we live
Era:

Target audience:
Theoretical
This one is likely going to be controversial with someone, which I fully admit is true. It
is
controversial. But that doesn’t mean it’s necessarily wrong.
Looking at the Xerox Alto, the computer that inspired Apple to create the Macintosh, as a machine that could be used to lay out and publish things might to some degree fudge the “desktop publishing” definition for some, but the case for it is pretty strong. First, one only has to point to Xerox’s legacy in copiers and printers as being compatible with the needs of a publisher.
Additionally, computer historians who have researched this stuff in-depth, such as Ken Shirriff, have convincingly made the argument that the Alto represented a desktop publishing platform before desktop publishing was given that name, citing the fact that the handbook for the computer was actually laid out using the computer, the Alto’s typography capabilities, and that the publishing tools were commercialized, albeit poorly.
“The Macintosh owes everything from the WYSIWYG editor and spline-based fonts to the bitmapped display and laser printer to the Xerox Alto,”
Shirriff wrote on his blog in 2017
. “Of course, Steve Jobs deserves great credit for making desktop publishing common and affordable with the Macintosh and the LaserWriter, something Xerox failed to do with the Xerox Star, an expensive ($75,000) system that commercialized the Alto’s technology.”
If it’s good enough an argument for Ken Shirriff, it’s good enough for me.
An example of The Book Machine, as shown in
a 1983 issue of Practical Computing
.
2. The Book Machine
Platform:
Dedicated machine based on Sirius microcomputer
Era:
Mid-’80s
Target audience:
Professional
One of the earliest examples of a computer built around typesetting, this machine, produced by Prefis, could capably set type on a page at sizes between 6 points and 48 points, in a variety of forms—including paragraph and headline sizes. It produced disks capable of managing phototypesetting tools without needing any additional steps, meaning its use case was working with existing phototypesetting technology rather than its own separate thing like many DTP tools of the era were.
It was ambitious, but you very much paid for that ambition. At the time, it went for £5,980, roughly $8,000 based on exchange rates of the time—and £17,363 today ($19,129). Not cheap, especially for a machine dedicated to typesetting.
In a 1984 piece in the
FID News Bulletin
, the outlet tried to make sense of who the audience might be for such a tool, and came up with this:
So who will use the Book Machine? It is after all a do-it-yourself composition system and most authors restrict their role to writing and leave composition to printers. The answer Prefis believes is that there are many authors of technical and educational material who would prefer to format and arrange their own material.
This turned out to be correct! But they didn’t use the Book Machine, a non-WYSIWYG desktop publishing tool, to do it.
3. MacPublisher
Platform:
MacOS
Era:
1984-1986
Target audience:
Professional
Released just before the far-better-known PageMaker,
this early tool
was one of the first software-based desktop publishing tools for the Mac, being released a year before PageMaker and anticipating the interest in such a technology on the market. While nowhere near as polished as many later tool
44513083.article_summary:
本文回顾了20世纪80年代桌面出版软件的早期创新，重点介绍了10款可能被遗忘的软件。桌面出版曾在印刷行业引发革命，尽管随着印刷媒介的衰落，它显得有些过时，但每天仍有大量内容被排版。许多早期工具未能存活至今，包括一些具有开创性但未成功的平台和软件。

1. **Xerox Alto**：虽然严格来说不是专门的桌面出版平台，但其图形用户界面和排版功能启发了后来的Macintosh和桌面出版概念。
2. **The Book Machine**：基于Sirius微型计算机，专为排版设计，但价格昂贵，目标客户是专业技术作者，最终未广泛普及。
3. **MacPublisher**：在PageMaker之前推出，是Mac上早期的桌面出版工具，但不如后者成熟和知名。

这些早期工具展示了桌面出版的演变，尽管许多未能成功，但它们为现代出版技术奠定了基础。

data.title: The most otherworldly, mysterious forms of lightning on Earth
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了发生在雷暴上方的神秘大气放电现象，包括红色精灵（red sprites）、绿色幽灵（green ghosts）和蓝色喷流（blue jets）。这些现象属于瞬态发光事件（TLEs），由雷暴产生的强大电场引发，通常发生在距地50至90公里的高空。红色精灵是最常见的TLEs，由正极闪电触发，呈现为短暂的红光，形状如同根系或水母。2022年，摄影师在青藏高原捕捉到105个红色精灵，并记录到罕见的喷流和幽灵现象。科学家正通过结合业余观测和专业研究，努力理解这些现象的成因及其与地球天气系统的关联。这些研究不仅满足了科学好奇心，还有助于更好地理解地面上的风暴系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于TLE（瞬态发光事件，如红色精灵、蓝色喷流等）照片及相关现象的讨论

不同观点：
• **HK-NC**：根据个人观察，描述了蓝色精灵现象的外观，并指出目前似乎没有相关的图片或视频。他通过比喻（用画图软件模拟）来解释精灵的样子。
• **jacobevelyn**：提到文章中未涉及球状闪电（ball lightning），并提供了一个维基百科链接以补充相关信息。
• **chias**：回应前一位用户，提供了一个专门展示TLE照片的网站链接，认为这是比文章更相关的资源。
• **neuroelectron**：以讽刺的语气暗示这些发光现象可能是模拟出来的，而非真实存在，表达了一种怀疑态度。
• **pbarry25**：仅提供了一个存档链接，未发表进一步观点。
• **the_arun**：抱怨National Geographic强制要求输入电子邮件地址，偏离了讨论主题。
• **chasil**：提出球状闪电是否更为神秘的问题，并附上了维基百科链接以供进一步探讨。
• **mock-possum**：引用了一段关于喜马拉雅风暴中出现的罕见TLE（包括喷流和幽灵）的描述，指出文章中缺乏这些现象的照片。
• **eth0up**：推荐了一个YouTube视频链接，称赞摄影师的拍摄内容丰富且精彩，特别提到了金伯利地区的拍摄。
• **adolph**：提供了一个摄影师网站链接，认为该网站对精灵现象的解释比文章更好，并详细解释了精灵红色色彩的形成原因。
• **foxglacier**：认为高质量的摄影可能夸大了现象的视觉效果，指出这些现象在现实中可能不如照片中那样壮观，且通常在云层上方发生，不易被肉眼察觉。

补充讨论：
• **TheAceOfHearts**：提到文章未涉及球状闪电，并表示失望，特别是提到中国研究人员自2014年以来有视频但未公开发布。同时，提到几天前有新的球状闪电记录，提供了相关链接。

争议焦点：
• 关于TLE照片的真实性与视觉效果的争议（是否被摄影技术夸大）。
• 文章中未提及球状闪电，引发对不同发光现象的讨论与补充信息的必要性。

总结：讨论围绕TLE照片的真实性、视觉效果及其相关科学解释展开，参与者提供了多个补充链接以丰富讨论内容，并特别关注了球状闪电的相关信息。

44480363.article_content:
SCIENCE
The most otherworldly, mysterious forms of lightning on Earth
Scientists are working to understand the curious phenomena of red sprites, green ghosts and blue jets high above thunderstorms.
Red spites, a type of transient luminous event or TLE, appear in the upper atmosphere above a thunderstorm in Oklahoma in April 2025.
By
Isabel Swafford
Photographs by
Paul M Smith
June 26, 2025
Our atmosphere is like one big electrical circuit: Thunderstorms are the batteries that charge it up, and lightning is the current flowing through it. On the ground we see evidence of this circuit when lightning cracks and strikes the ground, or when it lights up deep inside a thundercloud, but high above the clouds lies a secret electrical zoo full of sprites, elves, and jets.
These fantastical terms refer to light displays called transient luminous events or TLEs that occur in Earth’s upper atmosphere during thunderstorms. “TLEs are mysterious, beautiful, and uniquely different from conventional lightning, yet they connect weather, space, and electricity in one dramatic moment. They occur high above the clouds, almost silently, and are invisible to most people—but they reflect powerful processes unfolding deep within thunderstorms,” says Hailiang Huang, a Ph.D. student at the University of Science and Technology of China who studies TLEs.
The very first photographic observations of these events in 1989 captured red flashes streaking across the sky in the blink of an eye. The displays were dubbed red sprites, inspired by characters in Shakespeare’s
A Midsummer Night’s Dream
, and a medley of other fairytale names followed, as researchers discovered new types of TLEs. Today, scientists are still working to understand these curious phenomena—what causes them, how often they happen, and what they can tell us about Earth’s atmosphere.
Red sprites, like these captured in December 2024 in Mississippi, are by far the most common TLE observed by both researchers and photographers.
A photographer snapped this image of red sprite lightning in June 2023 in Kansas. Some have described the flashes as looking like carrots or jellyfish.
What exactly are red sprites?
Just like storm chasing, some photographers have taken to sprite chasing, searching for elusive red sprites and other TLEs above nighttime thunderstorms.
(
See rare colorful lightning sprites dance above a hurricane
.)
Red sprites have been observed off the coast of Europe and over the U.S. Great Plains, but in 2022, astrophotographers Angel An and Shuchang Dong captured 105 red sprites, the largest number ever seen in a single thunderstorm in South Asia,
researchers recently
reported in the journal
Advances in Atmospheric Science
.
4th of July Sale - 25% OFF!
Magazine for all ages starting at $25/year
SEE SUBSCRIPTION OPTIONS
“Red sprites are the most iconic [of TLEs],” says Huang, the lead author of the paper.
They flash into existence for just a fraction of a second in a spindly root-like system of red streaks. The phenomenon is caused by positive lightning that strikes the ground, creating an electric field that reaches up into the atmosphere, about 50 to 90 kilometers above Earth.
On the Tibetan Plateau, north of the Himalayas, thunderstorms are very common. The dramatic changes in elevation produce intense convection in the atmosphere and the churning of wet air creates clouds—a rich laboratory for studying TLEs. Yet none had been recorded there until An and Dong’s storm imagery in 2022.
Huang and his collaborator
Gaopeng Lu
, an atmospheric physicist at the University of Science and Technology of China, developed a method to synchronize the videos and photos that An and Dong took on the Tibetan Plateau. Using satellite data and maps of the stars in the night sky to determine the timestamps of each video frame, the team linked around 70 percent of verified sprites to the parent lightning that triggered them.
To Huang, the results demonstrate the scientific value of amateur observations. “It’s exciting that this field brings together professional scientists and passionate amateurs, working side by side to understand something so ephemeral, yet so profound.”
Not only did the photographers capture a significant number of red sprites, the Himalayan storm also featured even rarer TLEs called jets and ghosts. The team found 16 secondary jets, powerful columns of often blue or purple light darting upwards into the sky, and at least four
ghosts
, green hazy glows that can sometimes hover above red sprites.
“While sprites [and other TLEs] may appear delicate and silent in the upper atmosphere, they are often linked to powerful, sometimes devastating weather systems,” says Huang. “Understanding them not only satisfies our curiosity about the upper atmosphere, but also helps us learn more about the storms we face here on Earth.”

  - [rock_artist] 指出不同国家和文化对儿童噪音的接受程度不同，移民和文化差异使得这个问题更加复杂。
  - [voxleone] 提出社会对儿童噪音的容忍度增加可能与出生率下降和儿童在社会中的象征价值增加有关。

  - [bartread] 分享了个别儿童持续尖叫导致困扰的例子，认为虽然大多数儿童噪音可以容忍，但极端情况仍需处理。
  - [Aurornis] 质疑是否真有“趋势”存在，认为互联网上收集的个别故事不能代表整体社会现象。
  - [Apreche] 自述可能有噪音敏感症，希望儿童噪音不要在自己附近发生。

补充讨论：
- **对儿童噪音的健康影响**：
  - [didibus] 提出是否存在科学证据证明儿童噪音对成人健康的影响，这可能是一个值得研究的领域。
  
- **对儿童户外活动的期望**：
  - [GuinansEyebrows] 回顾过去儿童在户外活动的普遍性，希望社会能重新认识到让儿童参与社会互动的重要性。

- **儿童噪音的合理界限**：不同评论者在儿童噪音的可接受程度和场合上存在分歧，部分人强调需要设置界限，而另一些人则认为应更加包容。

In Defense of Outdoor Play
Katherine Johnson Martinko
Jul 09, 2025

Source: Shutterstock
There was a heated debate in Amsterdam recently over whether children should be allowed to continue playing inside a neighborhood soccer cage. Some residents complained that it was too noisy and demanded the cage be reduced in size. Others argued that the noise of children playing was normal and healthy, and the case should stay as is. The case went to court, and the supporters won out. The cage stayed.
Following the decision, Amsterdam’s sports advisory council, the Sportraad,
published a report
stating that the sound of children playing should not be considered a nuisance. It called the noise a “natural, welcome, and unavoidable part of life,” and recommended that bylaws be changed so that “the sound of playing children was no longer a valid reason for complaint by vexed neighbours.” Doing so would help prevent playground closures due to complaints (
via The Guardian
).
This is welcome news to any parent. Raising kids is hard enough, but it’s even harder when you’re a parent who is trying to reduce a child’s screen time, increase their hours of outdoor play, and somehow
keep them quiet
at the same time. That can feel like a near impossibility, particularly in urban settings where homes are clustered near parks, and where small outdoor spaces are shared by kids of all ages.
Subscribe
This Is Not Just Amsterdam
Noise complaints about kids playing outdoors are becoming all too frequent. A Toronto mother
received an anonymous letter
telling her to “correct” her four sons for screaming and to keep them constantly supervised or take them to the park. In Vancouver, a popular playground slide was removed after neighbors
complained
it was too loud. In Calgary, a man installed a chirping alarm that went off every time the kids next door whooped or shouted in their own backyard. The kids’ mother
told a news reporter
, “I thought it was an annoying bird, and it wasn’t until we were out in the back that I realized it was when the kids were just playing.”
In Texas, a family was
sued by neighbors
who said the noise from their four kids playing in a backyard playhouse violated their “tranquil quality of life.” In Long Island, parents were
cited
for violating a noise ordinance because their daughters squealed while swimming in a pool. That summons was later dismissed, but the message was clear: your children’s joy is a problem.
Cities across North America and the UK have
restricted
street
sports
, citing noise, “
probable harm
,” and safety concerns. In Mississauga, Canada, officials
upheld a ban
on all street play. In the UK, London has more than 7,000 signs
forbidding ball games
across
housing estates, limiting the movement and activity of an estimated half a million children, despite nearly 53% of British kids failing to meet the recommended 60 minutes of daily exercise. The list goes on.
Understanding the Trend
Several years ago, the
New York Times
reported
on rising hostility toward child play noise in Japan. There’s even a crowdsourced website where people log complaints about “neighborhoods inhabited by stupid parents who let their children play on roads and parking lots.” Experts believe this growing intolerance reflects the country’s aging population. As one demographer put it, “fewer children makes people less accustomed to hearing the noise they naturally make,” which
leads
to more complaints, discourages families from having children, and reinforces a vicious cycle of demographic decline.
It’s easy to become annoyed by noise if you don’t spend time around children. When most kids are indoors, in cars, or in structured activities, and when fewer adults live near families, even ordinary sounds of outdoor play can feel disruptive.
But play is
essential
, and play is loud. Kids yelp, squeal, cheer, chant, and crash into things. That’s how they express joy, test boundaries, and connect with one another. Trying to suppress that energy by demanding silence or defaulting to screens is
damaging
.
Of course, there’s a difference between regular noisy play and gratuitous screaming, which parents should minimize. Reasonable rules are fair: no shouting early in the morning or late at night. But adults also need to recalibrate. The sound of children playing should not be treated as pollution. It is the sound of a healthy, functioning community.
Whether we want to admit it or not, many adults still cling to the old idea that “children should be seen, not heard.” That’s part of why screen-based entertainment has taken over. It’s quiet. It’s controlled. It keeps kids docile. But quiet does not mean well. A child staring at a tablet may seem calm, but it often comes at the
cost
of physical, emotional, and social development.
