44521814.article_content:
Exhibitions
news
Executed Chinese prisoners likely used in UK exhibition
Cadavers on display in 'Real Bodies' show were provided by Dalian-based firm known to have acquired corpses from police
Cristina Ruiz
25 January 2021
Share
The bodies in the exhibition have been stripped of their skin and dissected to reveal their internal anatomy
© jacquemart
An exhibition of preserved human corpses in Birmingham may have included political prisoners executed in China, according to British parliamentarians.
Speaking in the House of Lords on 12 January, Lord Alton of Liverpool said that the cadavers used in an international touring show called Real Bodies, which was seen at the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham in 2018, “were probably people who had been executed” in China.
The bodies on display were stripped of their skin, dissected to show a part of their internal anatomy and then infused with plastic, which gradually hardened, a process known as plastination.
They were obtained from a firm in Dalian, China which has used corpses acquired from the Chinese police, according to a previous investigation by the New York Attorney General’s Office.
The exhibition was discussed during a debate on a proposed amendment to a new British law which is currently under consideration, the Medicines and Medical Devices Bill. The amendment would require all human tissues and cells imported into Britain for medical or scientific purposes to be fully documented with evidence that they were obtained with the consent of the donor.
The amendment is the first legislative response in Britain to the findings of the China Tribunal, an independent panel set up in London to investigate evidence that the Chinese state is removing organs from prisoners while they are still alive as part of a lucrative black-market trade in organ transplants.
Real Bodies: The Exhibition travelled to the South Florida Science Center and Aquarium in 2020
© Photo by Damon Higgins/USA Today Network/Sipa USA.
In June 2019, the tribunal concluded that “forced organ harvesting has been committed for years throughout China on a significant scale” and that “Falun Gong practitioners have been one—and probably the main—source of organ supply”, adding that evidence of forced organ harvesting of the persecuted Uyghur population may yet emerge.
“It is extraordinary that such things can happen in the 21st century, but they are happening,” Lord Alton told the House of Lords on 12 January. “It is crucial that we discover the origins of the bodies that are used in these sorts of exhibitions, which I personally believe should be prohibited in their entirety. The idea that they can be paraded for macabre purposes should fill people with a sense of disgust.”
Real Bodies
is organised by Imagine Exhibitions, a US firm based in Atlanta, Georgia. According to the firm’s website, the show has “recently been updated with the latest scientific research on how Covid-19 impacts the human body”. It is available for hire internationally as a pre-packaged show.
The company did not respond to a request for comment.
However, in an earlier debate in the House of Lords last October, Lord Alton noted that “in 2018, we pointed out that the US organisers, Imagine Exhibitions, were unable to provide any evidence of consent for the use of these cadavers. The organisers merely said that the cadavers were unclaimed bodies obtained from Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company China. Imagine Exhibitions CEO, Tom Zaller, admitted in an interview that the bodies were ‘absolutely from China’ but added that there was ‘no documentation’ to prove their identities or to show they had agreed in life to donate their corpses in death.”
According to Imagine Exhibitions’ website, from 1999 to 2009 Zaller worked at Premier Exhibitions, another US firm which organised touring shows of plastinated bodies. In 2008, the then Attorney General of New York, Andrew Cuomo, reached a settlement with Premier which “brings an end to Premier’s practice of using bodies of undocumented origins in their exhibitions”, according to a press release issued on 29 May 2008. For future shows in the state, the company would be required to “obtain documentation demonstrating the cause of death and origins of the cadavers and body parts it displays as well as proof that the decedent consented to the use of his or her remains in such a manner”.
The press release noted that all of the corpses included in a version of the show then on display at New York City’s South Street Seaport were licensed by Premier Exhibitions from the Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company which, in turn, had “acquired [them] indirectly from the Chinese Bureau of Police”. The company was, the press release continued, “unable to demonstrate the cause of death or the origin of the decedents”.

44516317.article_content:
← Back to Home
← Back to Writings
The Only SaaS Feature You Should Be Building
7/9/2025
“SaaS is dead. The future is CRUD apps that act as a thin layer over data. The real work will happen through agents that interact with both data and people.”
– Satya Nadella (paraphrased)
I believe Satya is
generally
correct here. But before companies can get there, they have to solve one critical piece:
the action interface for human operators
.
This is a necessary step before the coming wave of headless AI. I’ll post about that next.
Why the Action Interface Matters
AI infrastructure and agentic layers are moving quickly. There’s progress on semantic layers, orchestration engines, eval frameworks, all great for admins and technical users. But what about the operators? The people actually running day-to-day workflows?
Here’s the truth: most operators aren’t prompt engineers. They don’t have time to fine-tune context, build evals, or craft perfect instructions. Their job is to keep the world moving, keep making the widgets.
What they need is simple:
A clean interface that let’s them
react to and confirm actions.
A way to
proactively ask the system to take actions.
Yet SaaS companies are still building AI for a rare technical user.
The Two Modes of Work
Almost all SaaS tools today boil down to two patterns:
Tasks/queues —
where operators work through a list
Proactive actions —
where operators drive work forward (e.g. scheduling, updating records)
Everything else (alerts, dashboards, comments) is either feeding into or enabling those two modes.We’ve seen a lot of focus on proactive UX: chat interfaces, canvases, dynamic UIs. That’s important. But what’s missing, what every SaaS company will need to nail, is the reactive side. That’s where the next big unlock lies: designing interfaces that let operators react without friction.
The New Paradigm: Reactive Agentic UX
Reactive UX means operators aren’t hunting around for what to do. They’re not juggling five separate interfaces. They react to actions and insights. They have a single, go-to agentic interface. The agent surfaces the right actions at the right time. The Operator Interface is where the work gets done:
Reviews, confirms, or adjusts what the agent proposes
Creates the building block for real-world (logistics, support, field service, deskless worforce, etc.), human-in-the-loop training
To work in heavy operations, this interface can’t just be a static list. It needs a few critical components:
It should support intelligent task queueing and routing, automatically assigning tasks to the right user or team with clear prioritization and status indicators like “new,” “in progress,” or “completed.” It should also alert operators when something actually requires their attention, eliminating guesswork or manual triage.
Next, it needs a robust context panel that consolidates all relevant metadata in a single view. Whether it’s order details, historical activity, agent recommendations, or chain-of-thought reasoning, operators should not have to jump between systems just to understand what is happening.
Action controls should be seamless. Operators need one-click confirmations or edits of agent suggestions, along with the ability to reject or override them when necessary. Every action should be recorded with an audit trail so there is never ambiguity about what was done, who did it, or why.
Collaboration must also be built in. That includes simple hand-off or escalation flows for edge cases, as well as lightweight commenting or tagging so other team members can contribute without disrupting the workflow.
Finally, the interface should empower operators to initiate agent actions directly. With predefined templates or smart buttons, they should be able to trigger common workflows like rescheduling a delivery or generating a new quote without having to write a prompt from scratch.In other words, a great Operator Interface surfaces the right actions automatically, provides clear and contextual information, enables operators to react in seconds rather than minutes, and maintains a clean record of everything that happened.
This is the bridge between CRUD apps and true agentic workflows.
What’s Next
If you’re building SaaS or agentic software today, this is the feature to focus on.
Build the operator action interface
Make it dead simple for operators to engage with agents… No prompts, no context-building, no friction.
Headless AI is coming. But this is the bridge we have to build first.

data.title: Koala: A benchmark suite for performance-oriented shell-optimization research
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary:
Koala是一个面向性能优化的基准测试套件，包含14组来自不同领域的真实壳程序，如CI/CD、AI/ML、生物学和人文学科，并附带真实输入数据，支持大规模和小规模的性能测试。主要目录包括：  
- **analytics**: 处理网络日志  
- **bio**: 基因组和转录组分析  
- **ci-cd**: 构建和测试开源软件  
- **covid**: 分析疫情期间公共交通  
- **file-mod**: 文件压缩、加密和格式转换  
- **inference**: 使用大型模型进行媒体推理  
- **ml**: 实现机器学习管道  
- **nlp**: 使用壳NLP管道处理书籍  
- **oneliners**: 执行经典和现代壳管道  
- **pkg**: 构建AUR包并分析npm权限  
- **repl**: 安全审计和Git工作流重放  
- **unixfun**: 解决Unix文本处理问题  
- **weather**: 计算和可视化历史天气  
- **web-search**: 爬取和索引Wikipedia数据  

Koala提供了快速设置指南，可以通过脚本、克隆仓库或Docker获取，并使用MIT许可证。贡献者可通过GitHub提交问题和想法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该使用Bash编写脚本，尤其是在性能可能成为瓶颈的情况下

不同观点：
• [meisel的观点] 认为如果脚本的性能已经到达Shell可能是瓶颈的程度，那么就不应该继续使用Bash编写，而应该选择更合适的编程语言。这暗示Bash在处理复杂或高性能任务时不够理想，应该选用更强大的编程语言来处理这些任务。

• [反驳观点] 有些人可能认为Bash在快速原型设计和处理简单任务时非常高效，尤其是对于系统管理员或需要快速执行的小型脚本。即便性能存在瓶颈，也可以通过优化代码或使用其他工具来缓解，而不一定必须切换语言。

• [中立观点] 另一部分人可能认为选择编程语言应根据具体场景决定。如果Bash已经能满足大部分需求，只是某些部分存在性能问题，可以通过混合编程的方式解决，即用Bash处理简单逻辑，而用C、Python等其他语言处理性能关键部分。

补充讨论：
• Bash的优势在于其简洁和与系统工具的高度集成，适合快速执行系统任务和管理脚本。
• 切换语言会带来额外的学习成本和复杂性，尤其对那些主要工作不是编程的系统管理员或DevOps人员。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该为了性能问题完全放弃Bash，还是通过其他方式优化或混合编程来解决问题。

Koala is a benchmark suite aimed at the characterization of performance-oriented research targeting the POSIX shell.
It consists of 14 sets of real-world shell programs from diverse domains ranging from CI/CD and AI/ML to biology and the humanities. They are accompanied by real inputs that facilitate small- and large-scale performance characterization and varying opportunities for optimization.

Benchmarks
Each of the top-level folders (except infrastructure) contains a benchmark set.
Please explore the individual benchmark directories for more details on their specific inputs, dependencies, and usage.
Benchmark
Description
analytics
processes real-world network logs to extract and summarize key events.
bio
performs genomic and transcriptomic analysis using population and RNA-seq data.
ci-cd
builds and tests open-source software projects.
covid
analyzes public transit activity during the covid-19 pandemic.
file-mod
compresses, encrypts, and converts various file formats.
inference
runs media-related inference tasks using large foundation models.
ml
implements a full machine learning pipeline using scikit-learn.
nlp
processes books using shell-based nlp pipelines from unix for poets.
oneliners
executes classic and modern one-liner shell pipelines.
pkg
builds aur packages and analyzes npm packages for permissions.
repl
performs security auditing and git-based development workflow replay.
unixfun
solves unix text-processing problems from the 50-year anniversary challenge.
weather
computes and visualizes historical weather statistics.
web-search
implements crawling, indexing, and querying of wikipedia data.

container from scratch

data.title: Could a Paper Plane Thrown from the ISS Survive the Flight?
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了从国际空间站投掷纸飞机的可能性及其飞行 dynamics。作者Maximilien Berthet和Kojiro Suzuki通过软件模拟和风洞实验研究了纸飞机从400公里高度（ISS轨道高度）以7800米/秒速度投掷后的表现。模拟显示，纸飞机在前3.5天能保持稳定，但由于低弹道系数，下降至120公里高度时，因空气密度增加而失控翻滚。风洞实验中，纸飞机在承受7秒高超音速风（马赫7）后，虽然机头弯曲并出现烧焦迹象，但未解体。实验证明纸飞机无法完整返回地面，但这种设计启发未来可用于如金星探测等任务中的一次性探测器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纸飞机从低地球轨道（LEO）再入大气层时的行为和物理特性

不同观点：
• **nickparker**：认为文章没有覆盖实际结论，强调了模拟与实验研究的主要发现，包括轨道衰减速度、姿态稳定性以及再入大气层时的严重加热问题，可能导致燃烧或热解。
• **peterlk**：同意纸飞机很可能在大气层中燃烧，引用了原始论文支持这个观点。

44521094.article_content:
Could a Paper Plane Thrown From The International Space Station Survive The Flight?
Space
10 July 2025
By
Andy Tomaswick, Universe Today
(kieferpix/Getty Images)
Sometimes there are profound questions in life that must be answered, like "What is the meaning of existence?", "Are we alone in the universe?" or "What happens if you throw a paper airplane from the International Space Station?"
Luckily, that third one has finally been answered, because of course someone would eventually.
A new paper
from Maximilien Berthet and Kojiro Suzuki from the University of Tokyo looks at "the dynamics of an origami space plane during Earth atmospheric reentry"
–
in other words, what happens when you throw a paper plane out of the ISS.
First, let's go over some technical ideas that are necessary to understanding this seemingly simple concept.
Related:
ESA Report Says There's Too Much Junk in Earth Orbit Trunk
Origami literally means folded paper in Japanese, and in this case the authors decided to make their paper airplane out of a standard A4 sheet of white paper. The end result looks like something a third grader would have made up to annoy their friend sitting in front of them in class, but with a lot more aerodynamic modeling.
Once the software model was made, it was time to put it to the test. The ISS orbits at around 400 kilometers (about 250 miles), so the authors decided to launch the plane from that height, and at a speed similar to that of the ISS itself - 7800 meters/second.
That speed might seem likely it would shred any plane made out of paper, but at 400 km altitude the atmosphere isn't thick enough to do much damage… yet.
That's actually the case for the majority of the descent back to the ground. From 400 km down to around 120 km altitude, the plane stays relatively stable, given the lack of air.
However, the plane descends very quickly due to its low ballistic coefficient, which is a measure of how well it can overcome air resistance. With its low ballistic coefficient, the plane rapidly slow, descending to 120 km in about 3.5 days.
On the slip side, a low ballistic coefficient would mean that, once the plane entered the atmosphere it would actually have a lower terminal velocity than something like a cannonball.
Illustration of a paper airplane, thrown from orbit. (NASA/ESA/M. Berthet & K Suzuki)
Unfortunately it never makes it that far, as, according to the simulations, at around 120 km altitude, the increased air density induces uncontrollable tumbling, essentially sending the plane into an uncontrollable flight path familiar to anyone who has ever made one of them.
But why stop at simulations when you have a PhD in Aerospace Engineering and can build a paper airplane for science? And why just build one when you can test one in a hyper-advanced wind tunnel on your university's campus?
The answer is you don't stop - which is why the authors built an actual paper airplane model (admittedly with an aluminum tail) and put it into the Kashiwa Hypersonic and High Enthalpy Wind Tunnel at the University of Tokyo to see what kind of aerodynamic forces their paper airplane could withstand.
They didn't go easy on their experiments either. Their one-third model paper airplane was subjected to Mach 7 winds for 7 seconds, similar to the forces experienced during actual reentry. This, unsurprisingly, bent the nose of the paper airplane back, but to its credit it didn't disintegrate – at least not in that amount of time.
There was also noticeable evidence of charring on the nose and wing tips, indicating that, if the experiment had gone on longer, the paper plane would have burnt up.
Ultimately, proving that's what would happen was one of the purposes of this experiment. There are plenty of mission architectures that could potentially use something similar to this paper airplane model – the LEAVES experiment for
Venus
exploration comes to mind, but there are also plenty of Earth observations that would benefit from a lightweight, stable platform to do their collecting from while burning up completely in the atmosphere at their end of life.
Mounting any such mission would require electronics and many other additions that would complicate the purity of testing a simple paper plane that a kid could have made it class.
But sometimes science is as much about inspiration as it is about exploration, and the results in this paper provide a nice mix of both.

data.title: Where can I see Hokusai's Great Wave today?
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 葛饰北斋的著名作品《神奈川冲浪里》目前在意大利的特雷维索Musei Civici博物馆和南特的历史博物馆展出，分别展至2025年9月28日和2025年9月7日。此外，该作品也在特里este的东方艺术市民博物馆和维罗纳的Palazzo Maffei博物馆展出（信息来自Instagram）。在美国，康涅狄格州的Hill-Stead博物馆也有展出（详见其官网）。还有55个地点也展出该作品。文章还提到可通过GitHub让博物馆或画廊列出展览信息，并可通过RSS订阅更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《神奈川冲浪里》（The Great Wave）及其相关艺术作品的讨论，涉及艺术作品的展示、复制及其文化意义。

不同观点：
• msephton：作为网站的创建者，提到该网站已变得更加自动化，并扩展到搜索新闻稿以获取相关信息。他还提到当前在东京成田机场的数字展览，并指出该作品的持续受欢迎程度。
• akkartik：分享了一个关于如何防止艺术品褪色的链接，并对该技术表现出兴趣。
• esperent：承认《Great Wave》的著名地位，但建议人们去探索葛饰北斋的其他作品，如《瀑布 penitence》和一些更怪异的艺术作品，并提到这些作品对理解现代日本漫画的启示。
• sharkjacobs：质疑观看原作相对于观看高质量复制品的优势，认为原作的重要性可能会影响观众的接受心态，但这也是博物馆和画廊展示策略的一部分。
• mNovak：推荐David Bull的YouTube频道作为了解这些版画及其历史的资源，并提到《Great Wave》在葛饰北斋生前已被广泛复制，因此很难确定某个印本是否为“原作”。
• OPBoot：建议支持像David Bull这样的当代艺术家，他们在努力保持传统日本木版画艺术的活力，并提供购买《Great Wave》复制品的链接。
• fusslo：分享了自己在康涅狄格州的成长经历，提到对当地艺术博物馆的新发现和未能及早体验的遗憾。
• aosaigh：对著名艺术品的临时展览运作方式提出疑问，包括博物馆是否支付原作拥有者以展出作品，以及运输的昂贵成本。
• seafoamteal：提到通过阅读小说《Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow》了解到《Great Wave》，该作品在书中起到一定作用。
• poulpy123：解释了《Great Wave》可以在两个博物馆同时展出的原因是因为存在约100份印刷品。
• xnx：分享了Google艺术与文化的链接，提供对《Great Wave》的在线查看。
• amarcheschi：提到亲眼见到《Great Wave》时对其小尺寸感到意外，认为其被称为“伟大”提高了期望值。
• burnt-resistor：回忆起《Great Wave》曾被用作《Applications of Digital Signal Processing to Audio and Acoustics》一书的封面，并误记其出现在90年代的高中AP微积分教材上。
• ChrisMarshallNY：提到《Great Wave》让他想起了“Is Abe Vigoda Dead?”网站，这是一种对持续在线状态的幽默类比。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：对原作与复制品的价值讨论，特别是原作的重要性是否仅仅因为其“重要”地位而影响观众体验。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：对艺术品运输和展览运作方式的疑问，以及对《Great Wave》文化影响的个人回忆和联想。

data.author: OnionBlender
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• **[jtc-hn的观点]**：认为AI工具（特别是类型预估工具）常常引入细微错误或不准确的函数名称，导致用户浪费时间去评估或修正AI的建议。这些工具虽然有帮助，但缺乏足够的上下文理解，可能会在代码的某一处做出修改，却导致其他部分出现问题，需要大量人工管理，打断了编码的流畅性。
  
• **[duxup的观点]**：对AI工具持较为积极的态度。虽然承认AI的建议并非总是完全准确，但认为通过主动探索和调查AI的建议，可以提升代码质量。同时认为，谨慎使用AI工具并主动承担责任是合理的做法。

• **[mertleee的观点]**：对AI工具的效果感到困惑，提到自己可能因为依赖工具而忘记了某些技术面试中需要的简写技巧，不确定是自己能力问题还是工具的实际效用。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的上下文理解不足**：jtc-hn指出当前AI工具在处理代码时，缺乏对整体项目的上下文理解，导致需要人为干预。
• **AI工具对编码流畅性的影响**：jtc-hn提到AI工具的错误建议会打断编码思路，增加额外的工作量。
• **主动探索与责任承担**：duxup强调使用AI工具时，主动调查和验证其建议是负责任的做法，并认为这可能带来更好的代码质量。
• **依赖AI工具的副作用**：mertleee担心过度依赖AI工具可能导致自身技能的退化，特别是在技术面试等场景中。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是否真的提高了编码效率和质量，还是反而增加了额外的工作量和管理成本。
• 过度依赖AI工具是否会导致程序员自身技能的退化。

总结：讨论主要围绕AI编码工具的优缺点展开，涉及其对编码效率、代码质量以及程序员自身技能的影响。不同用户对工具的实际效果有不同的体验和看法。

• **[duxup的观点]**：对AI工具持较为积极的态度。虽然承认AI的建议并非总是完全准确，但认为通过主动探索和调查AI的建议，可以提升代码质量。同时认为，谨慎使用AI工具并主动承担责任是合理的做法。

• **[mertleee的观点]**：对AI工具的效果感到困惑，提到自己可能因为依赖工具而忘记了某些技术面试中需要的简写技巧，不确定是自己能力问题还是工具的实际效用。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的上下文理解不足**：jtc-hn指出当前AI工具在处理代码时，缺乏对整体项目的上下文理解，导致需要人为干预。
• **AI工具对编码流畅性的影响**：jtc-hn提到AI工具的错误建议会打断编码思路，增加额外的工作量。
• **主动探索与责任承担**：duxup强调使用AI工具时，主动调查和验证其建议是负责任的做法，并认为这可能带来更好的代码质量。
• **依赖AI工具的副作用**：mertleee担心过度依赖AI工具可能导致自身技能的退化，特别是在技术面试等场景中。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是否真的提高了编码效率和质量，还是反而增加了额外的工作量和管理成本。
• 过度依赖AI工具是否会导致程序员自身技能的退化。

总结：讨论主要围绕AI编码工具的优缺点展开，涉及其对编码效率、代码质量以及程序员自身技能的影响。不同用户对工具的实际效果有不同的体验和看法。

data.title: Libpostal: C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: libpostal是一个开源的C语言库，用于解析和规范化全球街道地址。它利用统计自然语言处理（NLP）和开放地理数据，帮助将人类使用的非结构化地址转换为适合机器比较和全文索引的规范化形式。该库支持多种语言，并提供Python、Ruby、Go、Java、PHP和NodeJS的官方语言绑定。虽然libpostal本身不是完整的地理编码器，但可以作为预处理步骤，提高国际地理编码应用的智能性、简化性和一致性。安装过程包括在Mac和Linux系统上通过不同包管理器安装依赖并编译库。项目依赖赞助以持续发展地理空间NLP研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地址解析和标准化库（如libpostal）的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• [支持观点] 一些用户认为libpostal是一个强大且有用的库，能够在处理全球地址解析时提供良好性能，优于正则表达式，并且在多个项目中取得了成功。例如，[Ameo]和[alganet]提到libpostal在解析地址时表现出色，能够有效处理许多极端情况，且易于集成到不同语言的项目中。

• [质疑观点] 部分用户对地址解析库的有效性提出质疑，认为地址本质上是无结构的数据，无法通过解析或标准化来验证其有效性。例如，[kerkeslager]认为，唯一可靠的验证方法是将地址与全球地址数据集进行对比，而不是依赖解析库。此外，[shakna]通过分享自己在非正式地址系统中的实际经历，说明了在某些地区地址的非标准化程度极高，解析库可能无法处理。

• [技术细节和挑战] 一些用户讨论了地址解析的技术挑战和系统要求。例如，[jandrese]指出全球地址格式和惯例的多样性使得地址验证成为一个几乎无法解决的问题。同时，[claytongulick]提到libpostal虽然功能强大，但并非轻量级工具，需要大量的存储空间和运行时资源。

• [替代方案] 部分用户提到使用商业服务或其它库来进行地址和电话号码的验证与标准化。例如，[weinzierl]提到Google的libphonenumber库，并指出许多公司使用商业服务来处理这些任务。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了他们在实际项目中使用地址解析库的经验和挑战，例如[ttw44]在初学Web开发时遇到的困难，以及[RobinL]对libpostal在特定应用（如地址匹配）中局限性的分析。

• 还有用户提到相关项目和工具，如[gorgoiler]列举了一些用于处理日常事物的编码工具，显示出对这类工具的广泛兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 地址解析库（如libpostal）在处理全球多样化地址格式时的有效性和实用性，以及是否存在更好的替代方案（如基于全球地址数据集的搜索引擎）。

libpostal: international street address NLP
libpostal is a C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world using statistical NLP and open data. The goal of this project is to understand location-based strings in every language, everywhere. For a more comprehensive overview of the research behind libpostal, be sure to check out the (lengthy) introductory blog posts:
Original post
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap
Follow-up for 1.0 release
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap: Part 2

Addresses and the locations they represent are essential for any application dealing with maps (place search, transportation, on-demand/delivery services, check-ins, reviews). Yet even the simplest addresses are packed with local conventions, abbreviations and context, making them difficult to index/query effectively with traditional full-text search engines. This library helps convert the free-form addresses that humans use into clean normalized forms suitable for machine comparison and full-text indexing. Though libpostal is not itself a full geocoder, it can be used as a preprocessing step to make any geocoding application smarter, simpler, and more consistent internationally.

The core library is written in pure C. Language bindings for
Python
,
Ruby
,
Go
,
Java
,
PHP
, and
NodeJS
are officially supported and it's easy to write bindings in other languages.
Sponsors
If your company is using libpostal, consider asking your organization to sponsor the project. Interpreting what humans mean when they refer to locations is far from a solved problem, and sponsorships help us pursue new frontiers in geospatial NLP. As a sponsor, your company logo will appear prominently on the Github repo page along with a link to your site.
Sponsorship info
Backers
Individual users can also help support open geo NLP research by making a monthly donation:
Installation (Mac/Linux)
Before you install, make sure you have the following prerequisites:
On Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y curl build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
On CentOS/RHEL
sudo yum install curl autoconf automake libtool pkgconfig
On macOS
Install with one command via
MacPorts
:
port install libpostal
Or as follows with
Homebrew
:
brew install curl autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
Then to install the C library:
If you're using an M1 Mac, add
--disable-sse2
to the
./configure
command. This will result in poorer performance but the build will succeed.
git clone https://github.com/openvenues/libpostal
cd libpostal
# skip if installing for the first time
make distclean
./bootstrap.sh
# omit --datadir flag to install data in current directory
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
make -j4
# For Intel/AMD processors and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
# For Apple / ARM cpus and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] --disable-sse2
# For the improved Senzing model:
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] MODEL=senzing
make -j8
sudo make install
# On Linux it's probably a good idea to run
sudo ldconfig
libpostal has support for pkg-config, so you can use the pkg-config to print the flags needed to link your program against it:
pkg-config --cflags libpostal         # print compiler flags
pkg-config --libs libpostal           # print linker flags
pkg-config --cflags --l

data.title: IKEA ditches Zigbee for Thread going all in on Matter smart homes
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 宜家计划推出20多款Matter-over-Thread设备，以使其智能家居产品更简单、更便宜。公司将通过更新其Dirigera智能家居枢纽，增加Matter控制器功能并激活Thread无线电，支持新产品及与其他品牌设备的兼容。宜家还将重启其音频产品线，推出价格低廉的蓝牙音箱，如Nattbad和Blomprakt。新产品包括智能灯、传感器、遥控器等，逐步取代现有的Zigbee设备。此次更新使Dirigera枢纽成为Matter控制器和Thread边界路由器，未来将支持更多设备类型。宜家致力于通过Matter标准实现智能家居的开放性和即插即用，同时保持价格亲民。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IKEA从Zigbee转向Thread和Matter协议引发的争议和讨论

不同观点：
• WhyNotHugo认为，Matter是一个封闭的生态系统，依赖于公钥基础设施（PKI）和设备证明证书，且Thread需要支付专利费，这与IKEA声称的“更开放的生态系统”相矛盾。此外，这种转换导致与现有Zigbee硬件的不兼容，用户可能需要更换所有设备或面对网络碎片化的问题。

• gorgoiler最初对这一变化感到担忧，但认为Thread通过网格网络支持IPv6，有可能解决Zigbee和IP网络在同一环境下的竞争问题。他分享了自己使用Home Assistant和Zigbee设备的积极体验，并希望Matter/Thread能带来更开放和便捷的未来。

• nick__m质疑Thread相较于Zigbee的优势，认为Thread仍需要一个边界网关，这与Zigbee所需的无线电差别不大。他质疑为什么制造商不继续支持Zigbee，而是转向Thread。

• AndrewDucker希望Matter/Thread能解决当前智能家居设备之间的互操作性问题，特别是Google和Amazon对通用开关的支持不足问题。他认为这将使设备设置更加简便。

• whitehexagon对IKEA放弃Zigbee产品线感到遗憾，他认为Zigbee已经很好地满足了家庭自动化的需求，并质疑为什么需要新的标准。他表示这是他最后一次投资新的家庭自动化技术。

Thread count: Ikea is stitching together a smarter home
With plans to launch more than 20 Matter-over-Thread devices, Ikea is embracing Matter in a move to make its smart home simpler and more affordable.
by
Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
Jul 9, 2025, 9:00 AM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
is a smart home reporter who’s been testing connected gadgets since 2013. Previously a contributor to Wirecutter, Wired, Dwell, and US News.
Ikea is relaunching its
smart home line
in a move that will make its low-cost products work with other brands, with or without Ikea’s own hub. Starting in January, the Swedish furniture giant will release more than 20 new
Matter-over-Thread
smart lights, sensors, and remotes with “more new product types and form factors to come,” David Granath of Ikea of Sweden, tells
The Verge
in an exclusive interview.
Ikea is also
rebooting its audio offerings
as it seeks to fill the
Sonos Symfonisk-shaped hole
on its shelves. The first two models in the new line of inexpensive, easy-to-use Bluetooth speakers for the home are the
$50 retro-style Nattbad
and a speaker-slash-table-lamp, the Blomprakt, coming in October, with many more on the way.
Related
Ikea’s latest speaker lamp ditches Sonos for Spotify and inexpensive Bluetooth
What is Thread and how will it help your smart home?
Matter will be better in 2025 — say the people who make it
These new products are part of the company’s ongoing effort to make its smart home as simple and affordable for as many people as possible. “A couple of years ago, we made some strategic decisions about how to move on with the smart range and the speaker range and make an impact in an Ikea way for the many people,” says Granath. He points to the company’s learnings from working with Zigbee and Sonos over the last few years, as well as its involvement in founding and developing the new smart home standard, Matter. “We feel we’ve reached that point. There’s a lot coming, but this is all the first step, getting things in place.”
Last week, Ikea released an update, currently in beta, to its
Dirigera smart home hub
that turns the hub into a
Matter Controller
and activates its long-dormant Thread radio, making it a
Thread border router
. This means it can now connect to and control any compatible Matter device, including those from other brands, and control them in its
Home Smart app
. It will also work with Ikea’s new Matter devices when they arrive, which will eventually replace its
existing Zigbee devices
, says Granath. It’s a major step toward a more open, plug-and-play smart home.
The Blomprakt is an LED table lamp featuring a Bluetooth speaker integrated into its top. It’s part of Ikea’s new focus on smart home and sound as it moves on from Zigbee and Sonos.
Image: Ikea
Initially, Dirigera will only support
Matter device types
that Ikea currently offers — so, no robot vacuums, door locks, or fridges. However, Granath says that as they launch more smart home products, the hub will be updated to support more device types.
The Dirigera hub
already functions as a Matter Bridge
, enabling Zigbee-based Ikea devices to connect to larger
Matter ecosystems
like Apple Home and Amazon Alexa. With the update, it now supports
Matter 1.4
and
Thread 1.4,
enabling energy monitoring and the
ability to join an existing Thread network
, among other features.
While the full rollout is expected later this year, the beta is live now through Ikea’s Home Smart app, but some features will be limited, says Granath.
Matter unlocks interoperability, ease of use, and affordability for us
We don’t have a lot of details on the over 20 new devices coming next year, but Granath confirmed that they are replacing existing functions. So, new
smart bulbs
,
plugs
,
sensors
,
remotes
, buttons, and air-quality devices, including temperature and humidity monitors. They will also come with a new design. Although “not necessarily what’s been leaked,” says Granath, referring to images of the
Bilresa Dual Button
that appeared earlier this year.
He did confirm that some new product categories will arrive in January, with more to follow in April and beyond, including potentially Matter-over-Wi-Fi products. Pricing will be comparable to or lower than that of previous products, which start under $10. “Affordability remains a key priority for us.”
“The premium to make a product smart is not that high anymore, so you can expect new product types and form factors coming,” he says. “Matter unlocks interoperabili

data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了ACT 2018应用范畴理论研究学校的开放申请信息，并提及了数理科学与几何学的相互联系。文章还概述了一系列关于图解线性代数的博客内容，包括各集主题和研究方向，并邀请读者订阅以获取更新。此外，文章还宣传了对博士生的需求，并提供了其他翻译资源和相关讨论。文章最后列出了一些历史博客条目和其他活动信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于数学概念的解释及其图形表示的有效性，以及对相关内容更新停滞的遗憾。

不同观点：
• theZilber认为作者在解释简单概念时花费了过多篇幅，但后来发现这种图形表示帮助他更好地记住了诸如交换律（commutativity）等数学概念及其名称。他特别提到，图形表示让他第一次真正记住了这个概念和它的名字。
• dclowd9901通过引用网络漫画，提出了一个关于人类在匿名状态下行为的公理，即“人类 + 匿名 = 不愉快”，借此暗示某种普遍的行为模式。
• MarkusQ表达了对该内容曾经连载时的喜爱，并对该内容似乎已被 abandon（放弃）表示遗憾，特别是曾经和学生一起追随的经历。
• phforms分享了多年前阅读该内容时的启发，尤其是图形表示在形式推理中的强大作用，尽管没有在实际中应用这些图表，但认为这种系统展示了可能性，非常有趣。
• Xmd5a讨论了更技术性的内容，介绍了广义Transformer模型，并提供了相关研究链接，表明这些模型可以通过抽象图形手段探索机器学习。

补充讨论：
• lorenzo_medici的评论似乎与主要讨论点无关，更像是一种幽默或题外话，提到了对Claude Makelele的赞美，可能是在另一个语境下的评论。

争议焦点：
• 对于theZilber的观点，部分读者可能认为详细的解释是必要的，尤其是对基础概念不熟悉的读者，图形表示是否真的比传统解释方式更有效可能存在不同看法。
• MarkusQ对内容停滞的遗憾可能反映了一些读者对该系列内容不再更新的失望，但其他读者可能并不在乎更新问题，只要内容质量高即可。

data.article_summary: 英国国家犯罪局（NCA）逮捕了四名涉嫌参与网络攻击的人员，目标包括M&S、Co-op和Harrods等大型零售商。两名19岁男性、一名17岁男性和一名20岁女性在西米德兰兹和伦敦被捕，涉嫌违反《计算机滥用法》、敲诈、洗钱及参与有组织犯罪。所有被捕者的电子设备已被扣押进行数字取证分析。NCA表示，调查仍在继续，将与国内外合作伙伴合作，确保将责任人绳之以法。此次行动得到了西米德兰兹地区有组织犯罪部门和东米德兰兹特别行动部门的支持。受害者应通过政府的网络事件指引网站报告类似事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网络攻击的责任、技术漏洞以及犯罪者背景的讨论

不同观点：
• **djaychela**：强调了网络攻击对现代零售业务的连锁影响，以及管理层在应对这种危机时的巨大压力。即使管理层不直接负责技术部分，也会受到波及，尤其是当系统需要快速恢复以维持正常业务运作时。

• **gluten_guardian**：对网络犯罪分子的年轻化表示惊讶，并表达了对具体攻击手段的好奇，认为与过去简单的欺诈行为（如谎报年龄买酒）相比，网络犯罪更为复杂。

• **lyu07282**：提供了具体攻击方式的细节，指出攻击者通过伪装成员工，联系帮助台重置密码，进而获取权限并加密系统数据。引用了具体的事件来源来支持其描述。

• **clort**：对嫌疑犯位于英国表示惊讶，似乎暗示对攻击者地理位置的预期不同，可能认为此类攻击通常来自海外。

• **aaronrobinson**：怀疑攻击背后有外国支持，认为单靠社会工程学不足以完成如此复杂的攻击，尤其是在针对外国系统的情况下。

• **casenmgreen**：提到使用Tor网络的网站被屏蔽，导致无法访问相关信息，暗示攻击者可能利用了类似Tor的隐匿技术。

• **devwastaken**：持激进观点，认为所谓的网络犯罪实际上是系统设计缺陷的结果。主张通过更严格的法规（如要求软件由持照工程师开发）来减少漏洞，并建议对因漏洞被利用而遭受攻击的公司进行惩罚。

补充讨论：
• **技术漏洞的责任问题**：devwastaken的观点特别强调了系统设计和开发过程中的责任，认为科技公司应为其系统的漏洞承担经济和法律后果。

• **攻击者背景的争议**：clort和aaronrobinson对攻击者可能的地理位置和背景持不同看法，clort对英国本地攻击者感到惊讶，而aaronrobinson则怀疑有外国支持。

• **实际攻击手段的细节**：lyu07282提供了关于攻击手段的具体信息，展示了社会工程学在网络攻击中的关键作用。

争议焦点：
• **攻击者背景和地理位置**：部分评论者对攻击者可能来自英国本地还是海外存在争议。
• **系统漏洞的责任和解决方案**：devwastaken的观点与其他评论者形成对比，认为漏洞的责任在于系统设计和开发者，而非仅仅归咎于攻击者。

Retail cyber attacks: NCA arrest four for attacks on M&S, Co-op and Harrods
Expired
Cybercrime
Four people have been arrested in the UK as part of a National Crime Agency investigation into cyber attacks targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.
Two males aged 19, another aged 17, and a 20-year-old female were apprehended in the West Midlands and London this morning (10 July) on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
All four were arrested at their home addresses and had their electronic devices seized for digital forensic analysis.
They remain in custody for questioning by officers from the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit in relation to the three attacks, which took place in April this year.
Deputy Director Paul Foster, head of the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit, said:
"Since these attacks took place, specialist NCA cybercrime investigators have been working at pace and the investigation remains one of the Agency's highest priorities.
"Today's arrests are a significant step in that investigation but our work continues, alongside partners in the UK and overseas, to ensure those responsible are identified and brought to justice.
"Cyber attacks can be hugely disruptive for businesses and I'd like to thank M&S, Co-op and Harrods for their support to our investigations. Hopefully this signals to future victims the importance of seeking support and engaging with law enforcement as part of the reporting process. The NCA and policing are here to help."
Today's operational activity was supported by officers from the West Midlands Regional Organised Crime Unit and the East Midlands Special Operations Unit.
Victims of cybercrime should use the Government's
Cyber Incident Signposting Site
for direction on which agencies to report an incident to.

data.title: Red Hat Technical Writing Style Guide
data.author: jumpocelot
data.article_summary: 《Red Hat 技术写作风格指南》是红帽公司内部多个团队合作的成果，旨在为技术文档提供写作规范和词语使用建议。该指南涵盖语法（如主动语态、一致性、标点符号使用等）、设计（如标题、界面文档、字体使用）、语言选择（如避免误导性语言、使用包容性语言）、以及如何有效使用交叉引用等内容。此外，指南还包含一个词语使用词典，为技术写作中常见的词汇提供正确用法示例。该文档依据Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported许可证发布，使用时需注明出处并遵循相关商标规定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术写作风格指南的评价和建议

不同观点：
• perching_aix认为指南中的一些句子插入语位置不当，导致句子难以理解，且用词有误（如"reference material"应为"reference materials"）。同时指出网站不能“介绍”东西，应该是网站所有者才能这样做。
• dctoedt肯定了指南的部分内容，尤其是在教学中有帮助的链接和具体示例，但也指出有些改进建议（如删除"simply"）可能导致信息丢失，对某些读者来说不够清晰。
• markedathome提出与其他公司（如IBM、Apple等）的风格指南进行比较，指出这些公司也有内部印刷厂和风格指南，以保持一致性。
• kaycebasques讨论了技术写作指南中的“最佳实践”和“惯例”的区别，认为指南中有些内容只是为了保持一致性，而不一定提升文档质量，建议在团队中共享理解以加快讨论。
• freedomben高度评价指南，认为其详尽且有帮助，适合广泛的读者，而不仅限于Red Hat员工。
• AdmiralAsshat总体肯定指南，但质疑语法部分包含过于基础的规则（如主谓一致），认为技术写作者应已掌握这些基础知识，不应在风格指南中赘述。
• GLdRH认为第4.6节内容荒谬，可以直接忽略。
• david422建议利用AI分析写作是否符合风格指南，以提高效率。
• ban2ly认为指南无用，因为Red Hat不写文档。

补充讨论：
• 指南的实用性和适用范围是讨论的焦点，有些人认为其详尽且有帮助，而另一些人则质疑其部分内容的必要性和实际应用价值。
• 关于句子结构和用词准确性的讨论反映了ESL写作者和母语写作者之间的不同关注点。
• AI在技术写作和风格指南应用中的潜在作用也被提出，显示出对技术辅助工具的兴趣和期望。

asyncmcp - Async transport layers for MCP
Overview
A regular MCP Server but working over queues :
queue-based-mcp-example.mov
Quoting from the
official description
:
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs.
But a lot of this context is not always readily available and takes time for the applications to process - think batch processing APIs, webhooks or queues. In these cases with the current transport layers, the MCP server would have to expose a light-weight polling wrapper in the MCP layer to allow waiting and polling for the tasks to be done. Although SSE does provide async functionalities but it comes with caveats.
asyncmcp explores supporting more of the async transport layer implementations for MCP clients and servers, beyond the officially supported stdio and Streamable Http transports.
The whole idea of an
MCP server with async transport layer
is that it doesn't have to respond immediately to any requests. It can choose to direct them to internal queues for processing and the client doesn't have to stick around for the response.
Current capabilities
Transport layer : sns-sqs
Server : Transport layer that listens to a queue for MCP requests and writes the responses to a topic
Client : Transport layer that writes requests to a topic and listens to a queue for responses
Installation and Usage
#
Using uv (recommended)
uv add asyncmcp
#
Using pip
pip install asyncmcp
Basic server setup
Note : we don't support FastMCP yet. The examples in this repo uses the
basic way of creating MCP servers and client

Limitations
Message Size
: For SQS - message size limits are applicable (256KB standard, 2MB extended)
Response Handling
: Async nature means responses may not be immediate
Session Context
: Storage mechanism handled by server application, not transport
Ordering
: Standard SQS doesn't guarantee message ordering

Unit Tests

data.title: Measuring the Impact of AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
data.author: dheerajvs
data.article_summary: 这篇文章报道了一项2025年初关于AI工具对经验丰富的开源开发者生产力影响的研究。通过随机对照试验（RCT），研究者发现使用AI工具的开发者完成任务的时间反而增加了19%。尽管开发者预期AI会提升24%的速度，甚至在实验后仍认为AI帮助提速了20%，但实际结果相反。研究还探讨了可能导致这种减速的五个因素，同时强调该结果仅适用于软件开发领域，并不能广泛推广到其他领域或未来的AI系统。研究旨在帮助理解AI在研发自动化中的影响和风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在软件开发中的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• simonw 认为AI工具（如Cursor）带来的生产力提升具有较高的学习曲线，很多开发者在适应这些工具时反而会降低效率。研究显示，只有少数具有丰富AI工具使用经验的开发者能够显著提升性能。
• noisy_boy 提出可以将AI用作“摩擦消除器”而不是解决方案提供者，利用AI处理小问题如语法，同时保持主动思考，避免技能退化。
• kokanee 指出，评估AI对开发效率的影响很难精确，因为对比无AI参与的任务，AI参与的任务可能在后期产生额外工作量，导致难以准确衡量AI的实际贡献。
• NewsaHackO 质疑研究的资金和发表平台，认为该研究未经过同行评审，且花费较高，质疑其学术价值。
• heisenbit 认为AI可以帮助指出代码中的卫生问题，但也会带来额外的时间消耗，需要区分哪些是暂时性问题，哪些是实际改进。
• fritzo 表示AI帮助其应对快速变化的技术依赖和发布方法，认为AI是拯救开源项目维护者的重要工具。
• 30minAdayHN 分享了个人经验，认为AI帮助其在没有时间的情况下贡献开源项目，但也有一些PR未被接受。
• tcdent 幽默地表示自己已经忘记了如何写代码。
• Jabrov 认为研究样本量太小（16人），希望看到更大规模的研究。
• geerlingguy 表示AI工具在开源项目中增加了不必要的噪音，特别是在代码审查和社区管理方面。
• MYEUHD 提到AI生成的PR浪费了开源开发者的时间。
• nestorD 强调开发者对AI工具的熟悉程度可能影响其使用效率，经常使用AI工具的开发者可能受益更多。

补充讨论：
• 研究样本量小，可能影响结果的普遍性。
• AI工具在不同开发者之间的使用效果差异较大，经验丰富的用户可能获得更大收益。
• AI工具不仅影响个人生产力，还可能对团队协作和项目管理产生影响。
• 对AI工具的实际效果评估存在困难，特别是在长期影响和总体工作量方面。

争议焦点：
• AI工具在开发中的实际效率提升效果存在争议，部分人认为学习曲线高，短期内可能降低效率。
• 对AI工具生成的PR质量和其对开源社区的贡献存在质疑。
• 研究的方法论和样本量受到质疑，影响其结论的可信度。

Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
We conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to understand how early-2025 AI tools affect the productivity of experienced open-source developers working on their own repositories. Surprisingly, we find that when developers use AI tools, they take 19% longer than without—AI makes them slower. We view this result as a snapshot of early-2025 AI capabilities in one relevant setting; as these systems continue to rapidly evolve, we plan on continuing to use this methodology to help estimate AI acceleration from AI R&D automation
1
.
See the
full paper
for more detail.
Motivation
While coding/agentic benchmarks
2
have proven useful for understanding AI capabilities, they typically sacrifice realism for scale and efficiency—the tasks are self-contained, don’t require prior context to understand, and use algorithmic evaluation that doesn’t capture many important capabilities. These properties may lead benchmarks to overestimate AI capabilities. In the other direction, because benchmarks are run without live human interaction, models may fail to complete tasks despite making substantial progress, because of small bottlenecks that a human would fix during real usage. This could cause us to underestimate model capabilities. Broadly, it can be difficult to directly translate benchmark scores to impact in the wild.
One reason we’re interested in evaluating AI’s impact in the wild is to better understand AI’s impact on AI R&D itself, which may pose significant risks. For example, extremely rapid AI progress could lead to breakdowns in oversight or safeguards. Measuring the impact of AI on software developer productivity gives complementary evidence to benchmarks that is informative of AI’s overall impact on AI R&D acceleration.
Methodology
To directly measure the real-world impact of AI tools on software development, we recruited 16 experienced developers from large open-source repositories (averaging 22k+ stars and 1M+ lines of code) that they’ve contributed to for multiple years. Developers provide lists of real issues (246 total) that would be valuable to the repository—bug fixes, features, and refactors that would normally be part of their regular work. Then, we randomly assign each issue to either allow or disallow use of AI while working on the issue. When AI is allowed, developers can use any tools they choose (primarily Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet—frontier models at the time of the study); when disallowed, they work without generative AI assistance. Developers complete these tasks (which average two hours each) while recording their screens, then self-report the total implementation time they needed. We pay developers $150/hr as compensation for their participation in the study.
Core Result
When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts. This gap between perception and reality is striking: developers expected AI to speed them up by 24%, and even after experiencing the slowdown, they still believed AI had sped them up by 20%.
Below, we show the raw average developer forecasted times, and the observed implementation times—we can clearly see that developers take substantially longer when they are allowed to use AI tools.
Given both the importance of understanding AI capabilities/risks, and the diversity of perspectives on these topics, we feel it’s important to forestall potential misunderstandings or over-generalizations of our results. We list claims that we do
not
provide evidence for in Table 2.
We do
not
provide evidence that:
Clarification
AI systems do not currently speed up many or most software developers
We do not claim that our developers or repositories represent a majority or plurality of software development work
AI systems do not speed up individuals or groups in domains other than software development
We only study software development
AI systems in the near future will not speed up developers in our exact setting
Progress is difficult to predict, and there has been substantial AI progress over the past five years
3
There are not ways of using existing AI systems more effectively to achieve positive speedup in our exact setting
Cursor does not sample many tokens from LLMs, it may not use optimal prompting/scaffolding, and domain/repository-specific training/finetuning/few-shot learning could yield positive speedup
Factor Analysis
We investigate 20 potential factors that might explain the slowdown, finding evidence that 5 likely contribute:

data.title: FOKS: Federated Open Key Service
data.author: ubj
data.article_summary: FOKS（Federated Open Key Service）是一个提供端到端后量子加密的Git托管服务，数据在本地加密后再上传至服务器，确保数据安全。它支持联邦制，用户可以选择自建或托管服务器，并通过现代后量子公钥加密技术防止量子计算攻击。FOKS还提供加密的键值存储，支持存储短字符串或大文件。其团队管理系统允许创建复杂团队结构，支持跨联邦服务器共享加密数据。设备管理功能支持YubiKey，并可在设备丢失时撤销其访问权限。FOKS通过简单的密钥层次结构实现这些功能，使用签名链和Merkle树确保安全性和防篡改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FOKS系统的功能、应用及其在加密操作和团队协作中的优势和争议

不同观点：
• [maxtaco] 认为在2025年，进行基本加密操作仍需要大量“粘合”工作，尤其是当需要使用YubiKey等设备进行重要秘密的加密和备份时。他提出像FOKS这样的系统是必要的，且应是完全开放的，以便在无需支付租金的情况下构建任意应用。

• [WhatIsDukkha] 补充了背景信息，指出maxtaco是Keybase的原作者，现在正开发一个类似Keybase的开源版本，并提供了相关博客链接。

• [marcopolo] 对FOKS已经支持git表示赞赏，认为这使得从Keybase迁移git仓库变得非常方便。

• [ethan_smith] 强调了密钥服务中的“联合”机制解决了一个关键问题：在保持发现和验证便利的同时，防止中心化控制。

• [singpolyma3] 询问了“联合”机制的具体运作方式，假设实际团队数据存储在单个FOKS服务器上，并猜测是否类似于轻量级的单点登录（SSO）系统，用于团队成员使用自己的服务器。

• [pmw] 希望通过两个比较更好地理解FOKS如何促进团队协作：1) 与共享的团队Linux机器进行比较，强调了联合方面和“允许客户端捕捉不诚实服务器行为的附加数据结构”。2) 与去中心化的git服务Radicle比较，关注FOKS中git存储和秘密存储的耦合程度。

• [dannyobrien] 提供了之前讨论的链接，引导读者查看更多背景信息。

• [hofrogs] 对FOKS主页上的AI生成图像表示不满，认为这降低了该项目的可信度。

补充讨论：
• FOKS系统的开放性和去中心化特性是其主要优势，尤其是在团队协作和密钥管理方面。
• 讨论中涉及了具体技术实现的细节，如联合机制和数据存储方式，反映了用户对系统架构和安全性的关注。
• 争议的焦点包括FOKS项目的可信度和主页设计选择对其形象的影响。

FOKS
the Federated Open Key Service (in beta)
What Can FOKS Do For Me?
$
foks
git create secrets
Created: foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
remote add origin foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
push origin main
⏻ Initializing FOKS ... ✅ done
️☝ ️Indexing packfiles ... ✅ done
️⬆️ Pushing objects to remote ... ✅ done
To foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
* [new branch]      main -> main
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Git Hosting
FOKS provides a secure, end-to-end encrypted Git hosting service.
Your data is encrypted on your machine before it is sent to the server,
and the server never sees data or filenames in unencrypted form.
This means that even if the server is compromised, your data is safe.
FOKS is federated, so the git server can be one that
you host, or one that is hosted for you.
Additionally, FOKS uses modern PQ-secure public-key cryptography, so all end-to-end
encrypted data is safe from quantum attacks.
$
foks
kv put /secrets/vitals/ssn 123-45-6789
$
foks
kv get /secrets/vitals/ssn -
123-45-6789
$
foks
kv put -f /secrets/doc.pdf ~/doc.pdf
$
foks
kv get /secrets/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf
$
diff
~/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf && echo "the same"
the same
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Key-Value Store
Internally, FOKS implements git atop an encrypted key-value store.
Clients encrypt keys and values before sending them up to the server,
and decrypt them upon retrieval. You can access
this key-value store directly, which can store either
short strings, or large data files.

Federated and Generalized Team Management
FOKS provides a federated and generalized team management system.
You can create teams, add members, and assign roles.
You can also delegate team management to other team members.
Teams can be members of other teams, allowing for complex
team topologies that can mirror real-world organizations.
Morever, teams can cross federated boundaries, allowing
users on different FOKS servers to share data with end-to-end encryption.

Device Management with Full YubiKey Support
FOKS provides a device management system with full YubiKey support.
You can register your devices with FOKS and manage their access.
You can also revoke access to a device if it is lost or stolen.
Revoking triggers a cascading key-rotation across all teams you are members of,
whether local or federated. This keeps data secure going forward.
How Does It Work?
A Simple Key Hierarchy
To power applications like the Git and KV-Store shown above,
FOKS needs a shared symmetric key for all readers and writers
of the data, available only to the authorized devices, teams
users and keys that the authors specify. FOKS achieves
this natural application requirement with a simple key hierarchy.
Everything starts with base-level keys, like user device keys,
backup keys, or YubiKeys.
Device keys are generated on user devices
and never leave the machine they are generated on. They are protected
locally with system-specific encrypted stores where possible,
and passwords where not. Other base-level keys include backup keys
(for which a human-readable code is the seed), or YubiKeys.
Every user of the system has a sequence of per-user-keys (PUKs)
at the next level up the hierarchy. The secrets seeds for these keys are encrypted
for all available base-level keys. A PUK rotates whenever
a base-level key is removed.
At the next level up there are teams, which work much like users.
All members of the teams share per-team-keys (PTKs), which
are encrypted for the team's members, be they users (via PUKs)
or teams (via recursive PTKs).
Signature Chains
In FOKS, there are two types of
parties
: users and teams.
In both cases, there is a rotating list of constituents (be they
devices or team members), and as these constituents change, so
to does the corresponding active PUK or PTK. As such users and teams
share much protocol design and implementation mechanism.
In both cases, the set of keys that can sign on behalf of
the party changes over time, and it's crucial for security that
there is a careful accounting of these keys that resists
tampering by the FOKS server.
To prevent tampering, FOKS uses "signatures chains", a linear
chain of signatures that can be played back to verify
the ordering of signatures, and that each signature was performed
with a key that was valid at the time of signing.
Merkle Trees
When different parties or computers access keys for a party,
they do so via signature chains; they grab these chains from
the server and play them back to discover the current set of
keys that represent a party.

44510913.article_content:
Perplexity on Wednesday launched its first
AI-powered web browser, called Comet
, marking the startup’s latest effort to challenge Google Search as the primary avenue people use to find information online.
At launch,
Comet
will be available first to subscribers of Perplexity’s $200-per-month Max plan, as well as a small group of invitees that signed up to a waitlist.
Here’s what a New tab looks like for me on Comet
Image Credits:
Screengrab/Maxwell Zeff / Perplexity
Comet’s headline feature is Perplexity’s AI search engine, which is pre-installed and set as the default, putting the company’s core product — AI generated summaries of search results — front and center.
Users can also access Comet Assistant, a new AI agent from Perplexity that lives in the web browser and aims to automate routine tasks. Perplexity says the assistant can summarize emails and calendar events, manage tabs, and navigate web pages on behalf of users. Users can access Comet Assistant by opening a sidecar on any web page, which lets the AI agent see what’s on the web page and answer questions about it.
Comet Assistant in your email inbox
Image Credits:
Perplexity
Perplexity has released several products and initiatives in recent months, but none feel quite as consequential as Comet. The company’s CEO, Aravind Srinivas, has significantly hyped Comet’s launch in particular, perhaps because he sees it as vital in Perplexity’s battle against Google.
With Comet, Perplexity is aiming to reach users directly without having to go through Google Chrome, the most popular browser currently. While AI-powered browsers present uncharted territory for many users, Google itself seems convinced this is the direction browsers are headed:
The Search giant has deployed several AI integrations into Chrome
in recent months, not to mention
AI mode
, an AI search product with a striking resemblance to Perplexity.
Srinivas
said in March
that his goal with Comet was to “develop an operating system with which you can do almost everything,” enabling Perplexity’s AI to help users across apps and websites. Becoming the default browser for users can translate to “infinite retention,” Srinivas
said in June
, which would ostensibly lead to more requests on Perplexity.

Perplexity
That said, Comet is entering a crowded arena. While Google Chrome and Apple’s Safari hold most of the market, The Browser Company
launched an AI-powered browser, Dia
, in June that seems to offer many of the same features as Comet. OpenAI has also reportedly
considered launching its own browser to compete with Google
, and has even hired some key members from the original Google Chrome team in the last year.
Comet could get an initial leg up in the browser wars if a meaningful chunk of Perplexity users sign up for the product. Srinivas recently said that Perplexity saw 780 million queries in May 2025, and that the company’s search products are seeing more than 20% growth month-over-month.
Taking on Google Search is no small task, but Perplexity seems to have the right idea by launching a browser of its own. But the startup’s team may find it even harder to convince users to switch browsers than weaning them off Google Search.
Hands on with Comet
The most unique aspect of this browser seems to be Comet Assistant. During our testing, we found Comet’s AI agent to be surprisingly helpful for simple tasks, but it quickly falls apart when given more complex requests. Using Comet Assistant to its fullest potential also requires you to hand over an uncomfortable level of access to Perplexity.
My favorite way to use Comet Assistant, so far, is loading it in the sidecar while I’m browsing the web. Perplexity’s on-browser AI agent can automatically see what I’m looking at, so I can simply ask it questions without needing to open a new window or copy and paste text or links. It’s right there, and it always has the context for what I’m looking at.
Comet Assistant can see your web page

Perplexity

data.title: Diffsitter – A Tree-sitter based AST difftool to get meaningful semantic diffs
data.author: mihau
data.article_summary:
**Diffsitter** 是一个基于 **tree-sitter** 的工具，用于生成具有语义意义的代码差异，忽略格式差异（如空格）。它通过比较文件的抽象语法树（AST）而非文本内容来实现这一点。该工具支持多种编程语言，如 Bash、C#、C++、Go、Java、Python、Rust 等。与标准 `diff` 工具不同，diffsitter 能识别出代码结构上的变化，而非仅仅文本格式变化。

用户可以通过配置文件过滤 AST 节点，选择哪些节点参与差异比较。Diffsitter 提供了终端友好的输出格式和详细的日志记录。它支持多种安装方式，包括预编译二进制文件、Cargo、Homebrew、Alpine Linux 和 Docker 等。

示例显示，对于两个 Rust 文件，diffsitter 能准确识别函数内容的增删，而忽略无关紧要的格式变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语义差异工具（semantic diff tools）的应用和改进建议

不同观点：
• **jbellis的观点**：认为语义差异工具在处理语法不完整的文件（如编辑过程中的文件）时表现较差，因此在Brokk项目中选择了传统的文本差异（textual diff）。他提到了GumTreeDiff作为一个更完整和积极维护的选项。

• **vrm的观点**：对语义差异工具在AI模型监督中的潜在应用表示兴趣，特别是通过人机协作的方式，利用人工编辑作为未来模型实现的监督信号。他提到了在编码用例中的一些相关工作，并表示对不同领域的方法感兴趣。

• **esafak的观点**：建议开发一个语义差异分割工具，将大的提交分解为小的、原子的、有意义的提交，以提高代码管理的精细度。

• **pmkary的观点**：对esafak的建议表示赞赏，但没有提出新的论据或例子。

• **fjfaase的观点**：指出该话题曾在其他平台（如Hacker News）上讨论过，提供了讨论链接。

• **dcre的观点**：提到mergiraf.org作为一个使用抽象语法树（AST）解决合并冲突的工具，补充了语义差异工具的生态。

• **the__alchemist的观点**：询问是否存在反树坐（anti-tree-sitter）版本的工具，暗示对不同技术实现方式的兴趣。

• **Iwan-Zotow的观点**：关注语义差异工具在VSCode中的集成，显示出对实际开发环境中工具集成的需求。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个工具和资源的引用，如GumTreeDiff、AI模型监督相关研究、mergiraf.org等，显示出社区对语义差异工具不同实现方式的广泛关注。
• 争议焦点并不明显，但jbellis对语义差异工具在处理不完整文件时的局限性提出了实际的担忧，而其他用户则更多关注工具的潜在应用和改进方向。
• 用户对工具的具体实现方式（如树坐解析、VSCode集成）表现出实际需求和兴趣，提示了未来开发的可能方向。

44520438.article_summary:
**Diffsitter** 是一个基于 **tree-sitter** 的工具，用于生成具有语义意义的代码差异，忽略格式差异（如空格）。它通过比较文件的抽象语法树（AST）而非文本内容来实现这一点。该工具支持多种编程语言，如 Bash、C#、C++、Go、Java、Python、Rust 等。与标准 `diff` 工具不同，diffsitter 能识别出代码结构上的变化，而非仅仅文本格式变化。

用户可以通过配置文件过滤 AST 节点，选择哪些节点参与差异比较。Diffsitter 提供了终端友好的输出格式和详细的日志记录。它支持多种安装方式，包括预编译二进制文件、Cargo、Homebrew、Alpine Linux 和 Docker 等。

示例显示，对于两个 Rust 文件，diffsitter 能准确识别函数内容的增删，而忽略无关紧要的格式变化。

data.title: State of the Art: Economic Development Through the Lens of Paintings
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过分析1400年以来的63万幅绘画作品，探讨视觉艺术如何反映其所处的社会经济背景。作者开发了一种学习算法，用于预测每幅绘画传达的九种基本情感，并隔离出同一地点和年份作品共享的情感信号，控制了艺术家、 genre 和时代影响。这些情感分布提供了关于生活水平、不确定性或不平等的细微而重要的信息。文章提出了一种基于情感的测量方法，通过历史艺术作品来审视社会如何经历重大的社会经济转变，包括气候变化、贸易动态、技术变革、知识生产转变以及政治过渡。研究得到了多个机构和项目的支持。

This paper analyzes 630,000 paintings from 1400 onward to uncover how visual art reflects its socioeconomic context. We develop a learning algorithm to predict nine basic emotions conveyed in each painting and isolate a context effect—the emotional signal shared across artworks created in the same location and year—controlling for artist, genre, and epoch-specific influences. These emotion distributions encode subtle but meaningful information about the living standards, uncertainty, or inequality characterizing the context in which the artworks were produced. We propose this emotion-based measure, derived from historical artworks, as a novel lens to examine how societies experienced major socioeconomic transformations, including climate variability, trade dynamics, technological change, shifts in knowledge production, and political transitions.

主要讨论点：潮汐能技术的可行性、成本效益、环境影响及技术挑战

不同观点：
• barbegal: 四个涡轮机中只有一个能够在不维护的情况下运行六年，其他三个需要昂贵的维护，相比太阳能，成本更高，即使在苏格兰这样的地方也是如此。
• davedx: 涡轮机在水下无需维护的时长创下纪录，证明了其商业可行性。潮汐能根据潮汐涨落发电，并且由于月球周期与太阳周期不同，可以填补太阳能不足时的电力缺口。但潮汐能受地理限制，只有少数国家具有适合的地点，全球技术潜力仅为海上风电的十分之一。
• sneilan1: 担心提取潮汐能量是否会影响地球自转，虽然作为外行对此了解不多，但对这种可能性感到好奇。
• NotAnOtter: 对海洋中充满技术设备感到不安，这些设备最终会磨损、破裂并造成污染。虽然潮汐能比石油更好，且在太阳能和风能无法提供电力时提供电力，但希望放弃需要大量这类巨型结构的方案。
• KaiserPro: 海水具有腐蚀性，加上其中的沙粒和其他颗粒，会变得具有磨蚀性。但潮汐每天两次达到30公里/小时的速度，提供了强大的能量。
• Animats: 潮汐能只有在地理条件合适的地方才能工作，需要像海湾这样的地理结构。
• sgt101: 举例说明一个潮汐磨坊已经运行了850年，至今仍提供电力。
• standeven: 认为如果这项技术可行，会受到虚假信息、游说、政府繁文缛节和关税的攻击。太阳能、风能和储能可以解决大部分能源需求，但受到不公平对待。
• octaane: 只有1/4的涡轮机达到目标，虽然是一个有希望的里程碑，但质量控制需要改进。
• worik: 在新西兰有关于潮汐能的争论，担心涡轮机会对鱼类造成障碍，影响渔业，需要认真对待和调查。
• amelius: 提取潮汐能量会影响月球的势能，使其加速靠近地球。
• nick238: 讽刺地提到涡轮机可能对海洋生物造成伤害，引用风能观察网站的内容，指出旋转叶片可能对大型鱼类和鲸鱼造成威胁。
• JR1427: 认为潮汐能是“眼不见，心不烦”的问题。

补充讨论：
• 技术可行性与维护成本：barbegal和octaane指出涡轮机的维护成本高和技术挑战。
• 地理限制与全球潜力：davedx和worik讨论了潮汐能的地理限制和环境影响。
• 环境与生态影响：sneilan1、NotAnOtter、amelius和nick238担心潮汐能对地球自转、海洋生态和海洋生物的影响。
• 社会与政治因素：standeven提到技术可行后可能面临的社会和政治挑战。

data.author: zigrazor
data.article_summary: CXXStateTree 是一个用于 C++20 的头文件唯一依赖的分层状态机库。它具有流畅的构建器 API、基于事件的状态转换、零堆分配的高性能运行时，以及可选的守卫和动作。该库支持 Google Test 集成和代码覆盖率检测，设计上注重可扩展性，未来将支持嵌套状态和 DOT 导出。库的依赖包括 C++20 编译器和 GoogleTest，通过 CMake 进行构建和测试。当前版本提供基本的状态机功能，未来计划增加协程支持和完善的文档。该项目欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python和C++项目中的实现细节和技术选择

不同观点：
• [baymotion] 提供了一个相关的Python项目链接，可能暗示对该项目有兴趣或者认为其与当前讨论内容相关。

• [jeffreygoesto] 对项目的紧凑性表示赞赏，但提出了两个问题：
  - 关于声明中的"zero heap allocations"与代码中使用list、unordered map和moves之间的矛盾，质疑是否应为"state tree building后的zero allocations"。
  - 建议对于嵌入式应用，应将所有输入/输出和dot导出等功能分离到另一个库中，以便在小型目标中可以省略。

• [dgan] 对使用"pragma once"表示疑问，指出这在C++中可能不受欢迎或不推荐。

• [happyweasel] 简单表示支持使用vcpkg（一个C++库管理工具），未展开具体技术讨论。

补充讨论：
- [jeffreygoesto] 提出了对嵌入式系统中代码优化的实际需求，强调了在资源受限环境中减少不必要功能的重要性。
- [dgan] 提到了C++社区中对某些预处理指令（如"pragma once"）的潜在负面看法，表明在技术实现中选择合适语法的重要性。

争议焦点：
- "zero heap allocations"的声明是否准确，或者是否需要更具体的解释以避免误解。

data.title: Analyzing database trends through 1.8M Hacker News headlines
data.author: vercantez
data.article_summary:
本文分析了18年来180万个Hacker News头条，以了解数据库趋势。使用camelAI和ClickHouse数据库，研究了13种数据库引擎的受欢迎程度变化。结果显示：

1. **历史趋势**：PostgreSQL自2020年起主导讨论，MySQL在2012年前占优，MongoDB在2013年达到高峰后下滑。ClickHouse和DuckDB在分析领域迅速崛起。
   
2. **增长最快**：DuckDB增长最快，ClickHouse和Supabase紧随其后。尽管PostgreSQL年对年有所下降，但其3年增长斜率最陡。

3. **衰退引擎**：MongoDB、MySQL、DynamoDB和BigQuery等云原生数据库讨论度大幅下降，主要由于成熟度和开源竞争。

4. **加权参与度**：PostgreSQL在总分和评论数上领先，SQLite平均得分最高，显示其受欢迎程度。Redis引发高兴趣讨论，而BigQuery和DynamoDB评论较少，表明兴趣较被动。

分析揭示了各数据库在开发者社区中的地位变化和趋势。

主要讨论点：数据库流行趋势及数据分析方法

• [xnx] 认为按月分析数据过于波动，建议使用三个月平均值以平滑数据，使趋势更清晰。

• [Tepix] 指出SQLite在增长，但未被列入增长数据库列表，觉得奇怪。

• [kwillets] 认为Snowflake已经达到顶峰，并提到2023年与 inexperienced devs 和 architects 打交道的困难。
• [markwclancy] 批评将操作/事务数据库与分析/列存数据库进行比较，认为这种比较毫无意义，类似于比较锤子和螺丝刀。

补充讨论：
• [vercantez] 更新了加权平均分析，补充了SQLite到增长表，并修正了原帖中的错误。
• [esafak] 询问数据清理的处理方法，是否有有趣的发现。
• [98codes] 对SQL Server未被列入表示好奇，猜测可能是因为信号不足或名称问题。
• [zurfer] 提供了截至2022年的数据和更多图表及情绪分析，并表示将尝试更新更多近期数据。
• [bellareed] 推广了一个免费工具，用于深入分析Hacker News数据。
• [Aachen] 报告数据查询工具链接无效，并提出登录功能可能解决流量被判定为滥用的问题。
• [chickenzzzzu] 幽默地指出流行度下降与大规模裁员有关，认为人们正在退出“web技术”领域，部分可能转向AI。
• [xnx] 提到一个不相关的网站 https://www.camel-ai.org/，可能引起混淆。
• [nsbk] 分享个人经验，提到从MongoDB迁移到TimescaleDB（现TigerData）的积极效果，并计划在分析方面可能用DuckDB替代Snowflake。

争议焦点：
• 数据分析方法的合理性，包括时间粒度和加权方法。
• 不同类型数据库之间的比较是否恰当。
• 某些数据库未被列入分析列表的原因及影响。

这些观点反映了社区对数据库趋势的不同看法和对数据分析方法的讨论。

Analyzing Database Trends Through 1.8 Million Hacker News Headlines
July 02, 2025
How the analysis was done
I used camelAI with a ClickHouse database of every HN story to do all analysis. You can use it for free with no login
here

18 years • 1.8 million headlines • 13 database engines
Hacker News is a real-time barometer of developer excitement. I mined every story title from February 2007 to June 2025 and asked three questions:
How has headline volume for each database changed over time?
Which engines are accelerating the fastest right now?
Which ones are losing steam?
1 · Raw popularity through time
The chart below shows monthly headline counts for the eight most-talked-about engines, plus DuckDB (small base, big growth).
Click on the individual database names to toggle their visibility. Double click to isolate a single database.
PostgreSQL’s curve is a near-monotonic climb; by 2020 it dwarfs every other line.
MySQL dominates the pre-2012 era, then flat-lines.
MongoDB peaks around 2013, then slips as SQL engines add JSON support.
ClickHouse (2016) and DuckDB (2020) rocket up in the analytics renaissance.
Redis & SQLite are steady, underscoring their “invisible infrastructure” roles.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X平台（前身为Twitter）的CEO更替及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论认为CEO职位形同虚设，薪酬过高而不值得。例如，[spjt]开玩笑说自己愿意担任一个年薪600万美元的“无所事事”的CEO职位。
• 有人关注新任产品主管Nikita Bier的任命，并提到他与X平台上发布的一个模因可能有关联，暗示公司内部的人事变动。[hakanderyal]
• 对广告平台的批评，[nikolayasdf123]直言ads.x.com是运行广告的最差平台。
• 有人质疑前CEO Linda Yaccarino的实际权力，认为她只是个有名无实的角色。[calmbonsai]、[dekhn]、[eviks]都提到她缺乏实权，许多重要决策都不经她手。

补充讨论：
• 对公司品牌形象的看法，[Hoasi]认为X平台在品牌毁坏的过程中依然屹立不倒，尽管充满争议，但仍然保持了相关性。
• 对旧Twitter时代的怀念，[leakycap]表达了对旧Twitter社群氛围的怀念，认为现在的平台无法复制那种“所有人都在这里”的感觉。
• 对高层人事变动的讽刺，[alganet]将此次CEO更替比喻为“向雨神献祭以祈求好收成”，暗示这种变动可能是徒劳的。
• 关于Linda Yaccarino离职的具体信息，[throwaway150]引用了X上的官方声明链接。
• 对Linda Yaccarino职业前景的推测，[paxys]认为即使回到她以前广告和合作伙伴关系主管的角色，也比继续担任被架空的CEO要好。

争议焦点：
• CEO的实际权力和角色作用：评论中对Linda Yaccarino在X平台的实际影响力存在争议，多数人认为她只是个傀儡，缺乏真正的决策权。
• X平台的品牌和功能变化：有人对平台的变化持负面态度，但也有人认为它依然保持了相关性。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 技术问题，[petemc_]提到在点击链接时收到不当内容警告，虽然与主要讨论点无关，但提出了技术隐患。

整体来看，评论主要围绕X平台高层人事变动及其影响展开，尤其关注前CEO Linda Yaccarino的实际权力和职业前景。

Hayden Field
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
Month after month, message after message, the AI engineer was hearing from Meta recruiters. The recruiters were pestering him to leave his employer and switch over to support the company’s AI efforts, and they were offering a sizable salary package to do so. But he wasn’t so sure.
The engineer, who works for a startup that was acquired by a leading AI company and requested anonymity from
The Verge
, said he had heard from friends that the company expected a lot of personal sacrifices in exchange for its high salaries, whether on employees’ value systems when it comes to Al or work-life balance. Engineers there, he heard, were working around the clock to catch up with rival companies like OpenAl, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft.
With so many firms desperately scrambling for AI talent, Meta was offering between $1–1.4 million in total annual compensation (which is typically measured as a combination of salary, annual bonus, and amortized stock value) for many AI roles. But, he suspected, its offers might be less generous than they sounded — tied heavily to subjective performance metrics that could be weaponized against employees. And just as importantly, he wasn’t willing to give up a semblance of work-life balance and a healthy work environment to make a few hundred thousand dollars more. He didn’t pursue the opportunity.
In recent months, Meta has launched on an AI hiring spree after making its largest-ever external investment: a
$14.3 billion acquisition
of a 49 percent stake in Scale AI, an
industry giant
that provides training data to fuel the technology of companies like OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta. As part of the deal, Meta spun up a brand-new superintelligence lab led by Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang — and to staff the lab, it started poaching.
Meta has reportedly poached
as many as 10
of OpenAI’s top researchers and model developers, with some pay packages
reportedly
adding up to $300 million over four years, including equity. (Meta disputes this figure.) It’s also approached a slew of other top AI talent across the industry.
Ruoming Pang
, who heads up Apple’s foundation AI models team, reportedly departed for Meta, and at least two Anthropic employees and two DeepMind employees have reportedly joined the team as well. The goal is to secure Meta’s spot in the race to achieve artificial general intelligence, or AGI: a hypothetical AI system that equals or surpasses human cognitive abilities, and the moving target that almost every AI company is currently chasing at breakneck speed. Meta’s primary weapon is vast amounts of money. But some sources across the AI industry question whether that will be enough.
Meta, to date, has not been the most exciting destination for budding AI engineers
Meta, to date, has not been the most exciting destination for budding AI engineers. CEO Mark Zuckerberg has been trying to make up for lost ground in the AI race, having spent years and significant resources over-indexing on the metaverse while competitors like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon invested billions in AI startups and signed cloud contracts and other deals. The company’s Llama AI models often rank low on publicly maintained performance leaderboards; at time of writing, Meta’s first appearance on one such leaderboard,
Chatbot Arena
, was at No. 30. In May, it reportedly
delayed the launch
of its new flagship AI model as developers struggled to deliver performance upgrades, and executives have been public on earnings calls about the need to aggressively invest and shore up against competition. The Scale AI deal, and Meta’s subsequent sky-high budget for hiring AI talent, is Zuckerberg’s Hail Mary: paying a premium for some of the brightest minds in the AI world to safeguard Meta’s future.
But although Meta is plying AI workers with staggering salaries, a mountain of money can’t buy everyone. Anthropic and DeepMind have reportedly had far fewer defections to Meta than OpenAI has, and that’s been an ongoing trend. The reason, to those inside the field, is obvious: the AI world is filled with true believers, and even the biggest companies need more than a cash offer to get many of them on their side.

data.title: LLMs show cultural theory was right about the death of the author
data.author: dcre
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了文化理论中“作者之死”的概念与现代大型语言模型（LLMs）技术的关系。作者亨利·法瑞尔指出，20世纪中期的结构主义和后结构主义理论家如罗曼·雅各布森等人，预见了语言和信息系统的自主性，这与当前LLMs的工作原理不谋而合。尽管文化理论在20世纪末失宠，但其关于语言和文本自主性的观点在AI时代重新焕发了意义。莱夫·韦瑟比的《语言机器》一书试图复兴文化理论，强调其对理解AI技术的适用性。文章认为，要理解生成型AI，需要接受语言创造力与智力可以分离，文本不必指涉现实世界，而是自成一体。文化理论的结构主义理解为现代AI研究提供了重要视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对福柯早期作品的评价及LLM（大型语言模型）技术对结构主义复兴的影响

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为福柯早期作品（如《临床医学的诞生》和《规训与惩罚》）的常见翻译版本读起来令人愉快，但《性经验史》后期的作品由于受德里达影响较多，阅读体验较差。
• PaulHoule表示他一直认为LLM会带来结构主义的复兴，并且这一趋势正在显现。他指出，尽管乔姆斯基的“贫困刺激理论”曾经使“X具有语言结构”的观点受到质疑，但LLM的成功训练表明语言确实具有语言结构，结构主义因此复兴。

补充讨论：
• 对德里达的批评与推荐巴迪乌：PaulHoue批评德里达的同时推荐了巴迪乌，认为巴迪乌在解构文本时表现出极高的精准度，令一些人不满。
• 对乔姆斯基理论的评价：PaulHoue提到乔姆斯基的理论未能成为语言技术的基础，并指出在Zork游戏之后40年，尽管有Inform 7和Attempto Controlled English等技术，乔姆斯基的理论仍然未能在实践中完全实现预期。

争议焦点：
• 对福柯和德里达等后结构主义思想家的评价存在分歧，PaulHoue明显不喜欢德里达，但认可巴迪乌的解构方法。
• 关于乔姆斯基的“贫困刺激理论”是否有效以及LLM的成功是否意味着结构主义复兴，这也是讨论中潜在的争议点。

There’s a great anecdote about Roman Jakobson, the structuralist theorist of language, in Bernard Dionysius Geoghegan’s book,
Code: From Information Theory to French Theory
. For Jakobson, and for other early structuralist and post-structuralist thinkers, language, cybernetic theories of information, and economists’ efforts to understand how the economy worked all went together :
By aligning the refined conceptual systems of interwar Central European thought with the communicationism of midcentury American science, Jakobson envisioned his own particular axis of global fraternity, closely tied to forces of Western capitalist production. (He colorfully illustrated this technoscientific fraternity when he entered a Harvard lecture hall one day to discover that the Russian economist Vassily Leontieff, who had just finished using the room, had left his celebrated account of economic input and output functions on the blackboard. As Jakobson’s students moved to erase the board he declared, “Stop, I will lecture with this scheme.” As he explained, “The problems of output and input in linguistics and economics are exactly the same.”*
Subscribe
If you were around the academy in the 1980s to the early 1990s, as I was, just about, you saw some of the later consequences of this flowering of ambition in a period when cybernetics had been more or less forgotten. “French Theory,” (to use Geoghegan’s language) or Literary Theory, or Cultural Theory, or Critical Theory** enjoyed hegemony across large swathes of the academy. Scholars with recondite and sometimes rebarbative writing styles, such as Jacques Derrida and Michel Foucault, were treated as global celebrities. Revelations about Paul De Man’s sketchy past as a Nazi-fancier were front page news. Capital-T Theory’s techniques for studying and interpreting text were applied to ever more subjects. Could we treat popular culture as a text? Could we so treat capitalism? What, when it came down to it,
wasn’t
text in some way?
And then, for complex reasons, the hegemony shriveled rapidly and collapsed. English departments lost much of their cultural sway, and many scholars retreated from their grand ambitions to explain the world. Some attribute this to the
Sokal hoax
; I imagine the real story was more interesting and complicated, but have never read a good and convincing account of how it all went down.
Leif Weatherby’s new
Language Machines: Cultural AI and the End of Remainder Humanism
is a staggeringly ambitious effort to revive cultural theory, by highlighting its applicability to a technology that is reshaping our world. Crudely simplifying, if you want to look at the world as text; if you want to talk about the death of the author, then just look at how GPT 4.5 and its cousins work. I
once joked
that "LLMs are perfect Derridaeians - “il n'y pas de hors texte” is the most profound rule conditioning their existence.” Weatherby’s book provides evidence that this joke should be taken quite seriously indeed.
As Weatherby suggests, high era cultural theory was
demonstrably right
about the death of the author (or at least; the capacity of semiotic systems to produce written products independent of direct human intentionality). It just came to this conclusion a few decades earlier than it ideally should have. A structuralist understanding of language undercuts not only AI boosters’ claims about intelligent AI agents just around the corner, but the “remainder humanism” of the critics who so vigorously excoriate them. What we need going forward, Weatherby says, is a revival of the art of rhetoric, that would combine some version of cultural studies with cybernetics.
Weatherby’s core claims, then, are that to understand generative AI, we need to accept that linguistic creativity can be completely distinct from intelligence, and also that text does not have to refer to the physical world; it is to some considerable extent its own thing. This
all flows from
Cultural Theory properly understood. Its original goal was, and should have remained, the understanding of language as a system, in something like the way that Jakobson and his colleagues outlined.
Even if cultural theory seems bizarre and incomprehensible to AI engineers, it really shouldn’t. Rather than adapting Leontieff’s diagrams as an alternative illustration of how language works as a system, Weatherby reworks the ideas of Claude Shannon, Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts, to provide a different theory of how language maps onto

data.title: Seven Engineers Suspended After $2.3M Bridge Includes 90-Degree Turn
data.author: _sbl_
data.article_summary: 印度博帕尔一座耗资230万美元、长648米的高架桥在中途突然近乎90度转弯，引发广泛关注和批评。该桥本应缓解交通拥堵，但由于设计缺陷，变成了笑柄。七名工程师因此被停职，相关建设公司被列入黑名单。项目设计因公共工程局与铁路部门之间的土地使用冲突多次修改，最终导致不合理转弯。当局正考虑购买更多土地以修正问题，但将导致更多开支和延误。此事成为官僚内斗和妥协设计的警示案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：印度一座桥梁设计多次变更，最终呈现90度转角，引发的讨论涉及工程设计、文化差异、以及对基础设施质量的批评。

不同观点：
• [oc1] 认为印度人在面对工程问题时具有灵活应变的精神，不会直接拒绝项目，而是找到解决办法，类似于软件开发中的思维方式。
• [BitwiseFool] 分享个人经历，提到受游戏影响，曾认为桥梁必须是直的，直到现实中见到弯曲的桥梁，这种体验颠覆了他原有的认知。
• [Aloisius] 指出实际转角并没有90度，而是大约120度，并提供了地图链接以支持其观点。
• [geodel] 批评印度基础设施质量差，并将其与欧美对比，提到印度有两种人：默默忍受不便的多数人和在网上激烈捍卫国家形象的少数人。
• [rilindo] 提供美国芝加哥湖岸S形曲线的例子，暗示类似设计并非印度独有。
• [recursive] 分享本地一个三向桥梁的例子，说明右转角部分仅供行人和自行车使用，认为设计实际上还不错。
• [andysinclair] 提到希腊雅典有一座带有两个90度转角的桥梁，认为设计奇怪。
• [a012] 提到越南也有一个真正的90度桥梁，提供了视频链接。
• [taeric] 表示同情，认为设计可能是受到某些限制所致，但看到实际建成仍然感到震惊。
• [hanlonsrazor] 认为只要桥梁能完成其功能且司机以合理速度驾驶，设计就没有问题，并对工程师团队表示支持。
• [kylehotchkiss] 讽刺地提到承包商可以通过关闭旧公司、开设新公司来解决被列入黑名单的问题。
• [cjcenizal] 调侃工程师选择了错误的转角设计。
• [sys32768] 质疑这些设计者是否真的具备工程师的专业能力，暗示他们可能只是拥有工程学位。
• [FredPret] 提到在老游戏《Stunts》的编辑器中也曾设计过类似桥梁，将讨论带入轻松的游戏话题。

Ever had to make a 90-degree turn
on a bridge
? No? That’s the problem. In India, seven engineers just got suspended for designing exactly that.
A brand-new $2.3 million bridge in Bhopal, India, is going viral—not because it solved traffic, but because it bends at nearly a 90-degree angle. Now, seven engineers have been suspended, a retired official is facing investigation, and the construction firms behind the project have been blacklisted.
Videos by VICE
The 648-meter Rail Over Bridge (ROB) was supposed to connect Mahamai Ka Bagh and New Bhopal, easing congestion and slashing wait times for up to 300,000 daily commuters. Instead, it’s become a punchline and a cautionary tale.
7 Engineers Suspended Over Bhopal Bridge With 90-Degree Turn
Photos of the sharp turn, which appears midway through the elevated roadway, exploded on Indian social media, prompting disbelief and concern. Drivers expressed confusion about how to navigate the turn safely. Others wondered how the project even got approved.
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav didn’t waste time. “Seven engineers, including two chief engineers, have been suspended with immediate effect,” he said, according to
The Indian Express
. “A departmental inquiry will be conducted against a retired sub-engineer. Both the construction agency and the design consultant have been blacklisted.”
According to official records, the design for the bridge shifted multiple times over the past seven years, largely due to conflicts between the Public Works Department (PWD) and the Railways. The two agencies couldn’t agree on how to share land, and in trying to work around both railway property and the new Metro line, they ended up producing a final layout with an abrupt 90-degree angle.
VD Verma, the project’s chief engineer, defended the layout, saying his team had no other option due to “limited land space” and the proximity of the Metro station. But critics argue that no one should ever have signed off on a turn that sharp.
Internal PWD documents show the original 2018 plan featured a more manageable 45-degree skew. That plan was scrapped after the Railways refused to approve construction on its land. A second design attempted to accommodate the Metro line. A third version adjusted for alignment errors, though the Railways later admitted that the final result “is neither fulfilling the functional requirement nor safe for road users.”
Now, Bhopal authorities are discussing buying additional land to fix the turn, but that means more money and more delays.
For commuters who hoped this project would ease daily travel, the bridge has become yet another example of bureaucratic infighting and design-by-compromise. For engineers, it’s a high-profile reminder that bad geometry can turn into political fallout very quickly.

data.title: Woman and three teenagers arrested over M&S, Co-op and Harrods cyber attacks
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 英国警方逮捕了一名20岁女子和三名青少年，他们涉嫌参与针对M&S、Co-op和Harrods的网络攻击。这四人因涉嫌违反《计算机滥用法》、勒索、洗钱及参与有组织犯罪活动在家中被捕。此次攻击导致M&S线上订单暂停，店铺货架空置，预计将造成高达3亿英镑的损失。Co-op和Harrods也遭到攻击，部分系统被迫关闭。国家犯罪局（NCA）称此次逮捕是调查的“重大进展”，并继续与国内外伙伴合作追查责任人。M&S主席称此次攻击如“灵魂出窍”，但拒绝透露是否支付赎金。警方从嫌疑人处缴获电子设备进行分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：马克斯和斯宾塞（Marks & Spencer）遭遇的勒索软件攻击及其原因分析

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，攻击者通过冒充员工，欺骗帮助台重置密码，从而获得了初始访问权限。这种观点强调了帮助台在身份验证流程中的潜在漏洞。例子包括通过社会工程学手段获取密码重置：[lyu07282]引用的具体案例。

• 另一种观点可能隐含在描述中，即一旦攻击者获得了访问权限，Active Directory的配置问题导致攻击者能够快速扩展权限并加密系统。这表明Active Directory的配置不当或缺乏适当的安全措施是造成攻击成功的重要因素。

• 还有一种讨论点是关于勒索软件攻击的后果，即攻击者在获取全部访问权限后加密数据并索要赎金。这一观点关注的是攻击造成的直接影响和损失。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点可能在于责任归属。部分人可能认为帮助台的流程不严谨是主要问题，而其他人则可能认为企业整体的安全架构，特别是Active Directory的管理不善，才是核心问题。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，攻击手段涉及社会工程学，这表明除了技术措施外，企业还需要加强员工培训以防止类似攻击。

• 具体的攻击细节和技术分析可以参考相关博客文章（如[lyu07282]提供的链接），这可能为深入了解攻击过程和防范措施提供更多背景信息。

44523027.article_content:
Woman and three teenagers arrested over M&S, Co-op and Harrods cyber attacks
Disruption from the M&S attack continues and is likely to cost the retailer hundreds of millions of pounds.
Adele Robinson
News correspondent
@SkyNewsAdele
Thursday 10 July 2025 14:01, UK
Image:
A man walks past empty shelves in a branch of the Co-op in Manchester following the major cyber attack. Pic: PA
Why you can trust Sky News
Four people have been arrested by police investigating cyber attacks targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.
A 20-year-old woman and two males, both aged 19, and another aged 17, were detained in London and the West Midlands as part of a National Crime Agency (NCA) operation.
They were arrested at their homes on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
Money blog: Cost of renting over owning home is a lot
Electronic devices were seized from the suspects and are currently being analysed by forensic experts.
M&S
halted online orders
, and shelves were empty in shops after the cyber attack on the retailer earlier this year.
The initial hack into the retailer's systems took place in April through "sophisticated impersonation" involving a third party.
More on Cyberattacks

Businesses urged to strengthen cyber defences amid increase in Iran-adjacent attacks
Related Topics:
Cyberattacks
Marks and Spencer
Disruption is expected to continue at the retailer until the end of this month.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
3:14
From May: Why is M&S cyber attack so bad?
The Co-op and
Harrods were also subsequently targeted
by hackers.
Paul Foster, head of the NCA's National cybercrime unit described the arrests as a "significant step" in their investigation, which remains "one of the agency's highest priorities".
He added: "Our work continues, alongside partners in the UK and overseas, to ensure those responsible are identified and brought to justice."
The arrests, which took place early on Thursday morning, were supported by officers from the West Midlands regional organised crime unit and the East Midlands special operations unit.
Earlier this week, the chairman of M&S told MPs that the hack had been "traumatic" and like an "out-of-body experience".
Archie Norman, however,
refused to be drawn
on whether the retailer had paid any ransom.
"We are not discussing any of the details of our interaction with the threat actor, including this subject, but that subject is fully shared with the NCA," he said.
It is estimated that the cyber attack will
cost M&S up to £300m
this year.
